findings.title: A channel is stored as active and submit reports success before the counterparty has acknowledged
findings.source: live runs: omnia-open-noncustodial.mjs against Hawk v0.2.12 and v0.3.0
findings.summary: submitOpenChannel writes the channel into the local store as active, then asks the peer. When the peer rejects, the store is not rolled back and the response is still { success: true, acknowledged: false }. The local node therefore reports a live channel that the counterparty has no record of.
findings.impact: Funds are committed to a 2-of-2 output whose other party will not co-sign, so the value is unusable until the counterparty is made aware. Any router or UI that reads channel state sees an active channel and will attempt payments that cannot settle. acknowledged=false is easy to ignore and is not reflected in status.

repro.expected: Either the channel is not persisted as active until the ACK arrives, or the failure is recorded on the channel (for example status "pending-ack") and the RPC reports failure.
repro.actual: totem_omniaGetChannelState on the initiator returns status "active" with totalValue 100000000 for channel 0x8e3aac4a4d94b3b45ae5dc4f7317e7ea, while the responder returns "Channel ... not found"; submit returned success:true, acknowledged:false.
evidence: responder B: totem_omniaGetChannelState -> error "Channel 0x8e3aac4a4d94b3b45ae5dc4f7317e7ea not found"
the funding output is on chain and unspent, held by MULTISIG(2, A, B)
0.3.0: initiator reported status "active" for channel 0xe6863650602f6f7a3e1b99df1ebba8d1 while the responder returned "not found"
packages/omnia-host/src/api/methods.ts: channels.set(...) happens before requestPeerReply, with no rollback on non-ACK

fix.approach: Make the persisted status reflect what was agreed. Keep the on-chain funding fact, but mark the channel pending acknowledgment until the peer ACKs, and return a non-success result (or an explicit partial result) when the peer rejects. If the channel is left in pending-ack, give it a documented recovery path that re-sends the proposal once the funding coin is visible.
constraints: Do not hide the on-chain funding output; its existence is still true and needed for recovery.
Do not make the ACK authoritative for the on-chain state (the tx is already posted).
Do not change the funding script or state contract.
acceptance: A rejected open is not reported as an active channel by the initiator.
The initiator exposes a recoverable pending-ack channel that can be re-proposed and becomes active once the peer ACKs.
A normal open still results in status active only after the ACK.
verificationPostPublish: cd artifacts/canary && pnpm run canary run 44-omnia-noncustodial-live  # responder must report the same channel

findings.title: Unsolicited SPLICE_FINALIZED and VC_FINALIZED messages overwrite trusted channel state
findings.source: security audit OMN-NEW-001, verified against source at 8fa26907
findings.summary: The SPLICE_FINALIZED handler takes payload.channel from the peer message and writes it straight into the channel store. The VC_FINALIZED handler does the same for payload.factory and payload.channel, and deletes a channel on vc-close. Neither handler checks that the sender is the expected counterparty, that a proposal or acceptance is outstanding for that id, that the payload carries valid signatures, or that any chain evidence supports it.
findings.impact: Any connected peer can overwrite persisted channel or factory state with its own object, or make the host forget a channel. Exploitability depends on transport access control: peers are bound by their transport key from the DHT and there is no allowlist, so "connected" is the only bar. This is a source-level finding; no exploit was executed.

repro.expected: A finalized message that does not match a locally recorded proposal/acceptance is rejected, and state is only written after signature and chain verification.
repro.actual: lifecycle.ts writes the peer-supplied object unconditionally: channelStore.set on SPLICE_FINALIZED, and factory/channel set plus channelStore.delete on VC_FINALIZED.
evidence: fix proposed in PR #218 (peer-guards.assertSpliceFinalized / assertVcFinalized); 19 guard tests
no lookup of spliceAcceptances/vcReplies before either write

fix.approach: Treat a finalized message as a claim, not a fact. Require an outstanding local record keyed by spliceId or vcId, verify the finalized payload against that proposal (parties, balances, sequence, successor coin) and verify the counterparty signatures, then persist. Reject unsolicited ids instead of applying them.
constraints: Do not trust any object supplied by the peer as authoritative state.
Do not break the legitimate finalize path after a local acceptance.
Keep emitting the existing observation events on success.
acceptance: A SPLICE_FINALIZED with no matching local acceptance is rejected and changes nothing.
A VC_FINALIZED cannot delete a channel that has no outstanding close acceptance.
A legitimate finalize still persists and becomes active.
verificationPostPublish: cd artifacts/canary && pnpm composition

findings.title: FACTORY_FUNDING_REQUEST signs an arbitrary peer-supplied digest
findings.source: security audit OMN-NEW-004, verified against source at 8fa26907
findings.summary: The FACTORY_FUNDING_REQUEST handler takes payload.digest, reserves a WOTS leaf, signs those exact bytes and returns the signature. It does not require an authorized pending factory, does not verify the proposed transaction, and does not bind the digest to a funding coin or to a locally initiated funding round. The host signs with the same tree it uses for other operations.
findings.impact: A connected peer can use the host as a signing oracle: any 32-byte digest it chooses gets a valid WOTS signature, consuming key material. Whether a returned signature can authorize a malicious on-chain spend was not demonstrated end to end; the missing binding is the defect either way.

repro.expected: A funding signature is produced only for a digest the host derived itself for a funding round it is part of.
repro.actual: The handler signs payload.digest after only checking that a local bundle exists.
evidence: fix proposed in PR #218 (resolveFactoryFundingTarget binds the digest to an accepted factory and a participant peer)
packages/omnia-host/src/lifecycle.ts:394 — onFactoryMessage returns early only if !factories || !localBundle

fix.approach: Derive the digest locally from the pending factory proposal and funding coin, compare it to the request, and sign only on a match. Require an outstanding funding round with a known counterparty. Never sign an opaque digest supplied by a peer.
constraints: Do not keep an arbitrary-digest path behind a flag.
Do not reserve a leaf before the digest is validated (a rejected request must not burn key material).
acceptance: A request whose digest does not match the locally computed funding digest is rejected without reserving a leaf.
A request with no outstanding funding round is rejected.
The legitimate round still produces a valid signature.

findings.title: Factory proposal still signs a peer-controlled commitment
findings.source: re-audit R-001, verified against source at 5d8c427b
findings.summary: CAN-010 closed the FACTORY_FUNDING_REQUEST oracle by binding the digest to an accepted factory, but a second signing path remains. FACTORY_PROPOSAL carries a peer-supplied ChannelFactory; the host calls acceptFactory(factory), which converts factory.pendingCommitment to bytes and signs it. Nothing reconstructs the funding transaction or checks that the commitment is what this participant agreed to fund.
findings.impact: A peer that can submit a proposal naming the local signer can solicit a WOTS signature over an attacker-chosen commitment. That signature is a factory funding witness, so it is the material that authorises spending the participant coin. Source-level finding; no exploit executed.

repro.expected: The commitment is derived locally from validated factory terms and funding transaction bytes; a proposal whose commitment does not match is rejected before a leaf is reserved.
repro.actual: acceptFactory signs factory.pendingCommitment exactly as supplied in the proposal.
evidence: fix proposed in PR #222: proposal carries funding materials; the acceptor rebuilds the funding tx and signs only the derived commitment
packages/omnia-factory/src/factory.ts:517 — Buffer.from(factory.pendingCommitment, "hex") is signed by leaseSign
no reconstruction of the funding draft in the accept path

fix.approach: Make the acceptor derive the commitment: rebuild the funding transaction from the proposal terms and funding materials with buildFactoryOpening, compare its pendingCommitment to the proposal, and sign only the locally derived value. Require the proposal to carry the funding materials it was built from.
constraints: Do not sign a commitment that is only peer-supplied.
Do not reserve a WOTS leaf before the commitment is verified.
Keep the legitimate single-proposer flow working end to end.
acceptance: A proposal whose commitment differs from the locally rebuilt funding transaction is rejected.
A legitimate proposal still produces an accepted factory with both opening signatures.
Covered by a two-host prepare → sign → finalize test.

findings.title: Omnia writes atom amounts with MiniNumber scale 0, encoding channel values 10^44 times too large
findings.source: two-host S4 run (`openChannel` threw `Cannot convert 0.2 to a BigInt`) reviewed against minima-global/Minima `objects/Coin.java`, `objects/base/MiniNumber.java` and `objects/Transaction.java`
findings.summary: Minima has one amount type, `MiniNumber`: JSON reports it as decimal MINIMA text ("0.2"), while the binary transaction stores `(unscaled, scale)` with value = unscaled x 10^-scale. Omnia kept channel maths in atoms but its canonical serializer wrote atom integers with scale 0, so a 0.2 MINIMA channel was encoded as 2x10^43 MINIMA. Separately, the RPC provider normalised its coin amounts to atoms while Hosted, Lookup and Composite providers stayed decimal, so `ChainStateProvider.getCoins/getCoin` no longer had a single unit contract.
findings.impact: Every non-trivial channel funding/update/settlement draft was invalid: `Transaction.checkValid()` requires 0 < amount <= 1,000,000,000 and rejects the encoded value as an invalid Minima amount. The S4 run failed earlier, at `BigInt("0.2")`, which masked the encoding fault. Consumers that expected node decimal text (tx-builder coin selection and serialisation, the extension's `TOTEM_GET_COINS` and selection, edge-adapters and realtime balances) would have been inflated by 10^44 once a provider returned atoms; a composite fallback flipped the unit mid-application.

repro.expected: input/output amount is `MiniNumber(unscaled = 2x10^43, scale = 44)`, which Java reads as 0.2 MINIMA and accepts.
repro.actual: the amount was written as `MiniNumber(unscaled = 2x10^43, scale = 0)`, which Java reads as 2x10^43 MINIMA; `isValidMinimaValue()` rejects it.
evidence: build a funding draft for 0.2 MINIMA (`totalValue = 2e43` atoms) and decode the serialized coin amount: `buildFundingTx(...)` -> `omniaDraftToCanonicalMinimaBytes(...)`
packages/omnia/src/transactions.ts: serializeCoinForMinima wrote `writeMiniNumberLocal(opts.amount)` with the default scale 0
packages/chain-provider/src/providers/minima-rpc.ts: getCoins/getCoin returned atoms while hosted.ts and lookup-client.ts returned decimal

fix.approach: Define one contract: providers return node-native decimal text; `@totemsdk/core` owns `amountToAtoms`/`atomsToAmount`/`coinAmountAtoms`; Omnia converts once at its boundary and writes every coin amount as `MiniNumber(unscaled = atoms, scale = 44)`. Value-bearing program state ports use the same scale and the scale is bound into the signed state commitment, so a signer cannot re-encode a port at scale 0. The Rust/WASM mirror uses arbitrary-precision integers and the same scale rules.
constraints: Do not normalise units inside one ChainStateProvider implementation; the interface has one unit.
Do not write atom amounts with scale 0 anywhere.
Bind the state-port scale in the commitment; a signed state must not be re-encodable at a different scale.
acceptance: getCoins/getCoin return decimal text from every provider and a composite fallback cannot change units.
A 0.2 MINIMA funding draft decodes to scale 44 with value 0.2 and passes the Java validity bound.
Value-bearing state ports round-trip at scale 44; counters/sequences stay scale 0.
Rust/WASM digest and commitment parity hold.

findings.title: Peer-scoped finalization stores peer-supplied factory, channel and splice state
findings.source: Omnia whole-family re-audit (2026-11-17), finding OMN-001
findings.summary: Every finalization message is now rebuilt from local state and stored from the rebuild, never from the peer payload. FACTORY_FINALIZED on an active factory may only fill funding references: sequence, state log, allocations and the virtual-channel set must match locally. Opening→opening verifies every supplied signature, rejects unknown parties and refuses removal. VC_FINALIZED derives the successor from the local factory plus the allocation set this host co-signed. SPLICE_FINALIZED rebuilds the channel from the local channel plus the signed totals and split. FACTORY_CLOSE_FINALIZED requires the settlement transaction this host signed and, when a chain adapter is present, observes the factory coin spent before closing.
findings.impact: A peer can no longer replace another participant's factory, channel or closure state with a message. Mutated sequences, logs, allocations, virtual-channel sets, signatures, balances or settlement transactions are rejected before the store is touched, so the host keeps its own accounting and only closes when the signed settlement is present and the factory coin is observed spent.

repro.expected: Every peer finalization message is rejected unless the resulting state can be rebuilt from local state plus a transition that verifies.
repro.actual: The stored factory/channel is rebuilt from local state plus the signed transition; the peer object is only an assertion. Tests cover active sequence/log/allocations/VC mutations, added and removed opening signatures, VC allocation/balance mutations, splice state smuggling and close settlement substitution (tests/unit/omnia-factory/src/__tests__/finalization-guard.test.ts, tests/unit/omnia-host/src/__tests__/peer-guards.test.ts).
evidence: packages/omnia-factory/src/factory.ts: assertFactoryFinalized active→active and opening→opening branches
packages/omnia-host/src/lifecycle.ts: FACTORY_CLOSE_FINALIZED sets status closed unconditionally

fix.approach: Derive the expected object locally for every finalization message: rebuild the factory/channel transition from the local copy, verify every participant signature and the state commitment, then store the rebuilt object rather than the peer payload. Reject unknown added signatures. Require a settlement artifact bound to the factory before accepting a close.
constraints: Do not accept a whole replacement object from a peer on any message type.
Do not weaken the opening→active checks that already exist.
Keep the wire format unchanged; this is a validation-boundary fix.
A rejected message must leave the store byte-identical.
acceptance: A matrix test covers every peer finalization handler against sequence, allocation, signature, identity and replay mutations; every case is rejected and the store is unchanged.
Factory active→active validates sequence progression and the state log before storing.
Opening→opening verifies any signature it did not already hold.
FACTORY_CLOSE_FINALIZED requires the settlement transaction this host signed and an observed spent factory coin.
The valid-path cases still succeed.

origin.note: Aliased to CAN-019, which tracks identifier-only finalization guards. CAN-007 covers the unsolicited-message half; this entry adds the factory active→active / opening→opening branches.

findings.title: A transferred VTXO keeps the previous owner's exit entitlement
findings.source: Omnia whole-family re-audit (2026-11-17), finding OMN-003
findings.summary: transferVtxo verifies `params.exitEntitlement` against the input VTXO, then copies the same object onto the output VTXO, whose owner and vtxoId are both new. verifyVtxoExitEntitlement binds owner, vtxoId, amount and holderIndex, so the attached artifact cannot verify for the recipient — and the exit transaction pays the previous owner. The entitlement is also optional, so a transfer may attach none at all.
findings.impact: A recipient receives a VTXO with an exit that pays the sender, or no exit. Any consumer that treats the presence of `exitEntitlement` as proof of a recipient-executable exit can lose the value.

repro.expected: verifyVtxoExitEntitlement(outputVtxo, outputVtxo.exitEntitlement).valid === true after a transfer.
repro.actual: The entitlement still names the input owner/vtxoId, so verification against the output fails on vtxoId, owner and holderIndex.
evidence: packages/omnia-vtxo/src/transfer.ts: verify against `vtxo`, then spread `params.exitEntitlement` onto `outputVtxo`
packages/omnia-vtxo/src/exit-entitlement.ts: verify checks vtxoId, owner, amount, holderIndex

fix.approach: Build the recipient's exit from the output VTXO (recipient as holderIndex owner, output id, same amount) and verify it before returning. Either require an exit for a full transfer or make the absence explicit in the result so callers cannot mistake it for an executable claim.
constraints: Do not mutate the input entitlement into the output; rebuild it.
Partial transfers must not inherit an entitlement.
The exit transaction must still spend the same pool coin and preserve the remainder output.
acceptance: A two-owner transfer produces an entitlement that verifies against the output.
A transfer without an entitlement reports that explicitly and is never described as exit-ready.
A partial transfer cannot carry an exit entitlement.

findings.title: Vesting policy never enforces the vested amount before the end block
findings.source: Omnia whole-family re-audit (2026-11-17), finding OMN-008
findings.summary: The vesting case checks the cliff, then `if (ctx.block >= endBlock) return valid`; before the end block it computes `elapsed` and `span` and never uses them, returning valid for any positive `claimAmount`. The maximum vested amount at the current block is therefore never enforced.
findings.impact: A beneficiary can claim the entire vesting allocation immediately after the cliff. This is direct value loss for any VTXO using the vesting policy.

repro.expected: At block `< endBlock`, a claim above the linear vested amount is rejected.
repro.actual: Any `claimAmount > 0` is accepted once the cliff is reached.

fix.approach: Compute the vested amount as a function of block (`cliff`, `startBlock`, `endBlock`) and reject a claim above it; use the elapsed/span values that are already derived. Make the cliff and end blocks explicit in the result so callers can display the schedule.
constraints: Do not remove the cliff check.
Partial claims before the end block must remain possible up to the vested amount.
Do not change the policy shape without a migration note.
acceptance: A claim above the vested amount at the current block is rejected.
A claim at or below the vested amount succeeds.
At/after endBlock the full amount is claimable.

findings.source: Omnia host signing audit, 2026-11-18 (verified against 997b7f40)
findings.title: The host signs peer-supplied virtual-channel plans without rebuilding them
findings.summary: VC_PROPOSAL passes payload.plan directly to signVirtualChannelOpen/signVirtualChannelClose. Those functions check that the local signer is a factory participant and sign plan.commitment, but never rebuild the plan from the factory allocations/channel state. omnia-factory/src/coordination.ts already rebuilds with buildVirtualChannelOpen, compares commitments and applies an approval policy; the production host bypasses that path.
findings.impact: A peer can obtain a WOTS signature over a virtual-channel commitment chosen by the peer, without proving it is an authorised transition of the factory this host holds. The host also commits the lease reservation immediately.

repro.expected: The host rebuilds the VC plan from local factory state, rejects a mismatched commitment, and signs only the locally derived commitment after approval.
repro.actual: lifecycle.ts passes payload.plan straight to signVirtualChannelOpen/Close; only signer membership is checked.

fix.approach: Rebuild VC-open/close locally from the factory and channel state, compare commitments and ids, require an explicit approval decision, then sign the locally derived plan. Persist the approval and reservation so a retry cannot change the transaction.
constraints: Never sign a commitment that only exists in the peer payload.
Bind factoryId, vcId, parties and amounts to local state.
Persist the approved plan before committing the lease.
acceptance: A mismatched VC commitment is rejected before any leaf is reserved.
Signing uses the locally rebuilt plan.
Repeated proposals reuse the same approval/result.

findings.source: Omnia host signing audit, 2026-11-18 (verified against 997b7f40)
findings.title: Incoming splice proposals are co-signed without verifying the proposer signature or approval
findings.summary: onSpliceMessage calls acceptSplice directly. acceptSplice checks membership, quiescence, conservation and draft/params binding, but never verifies proposal.proposerSignature and has no spending approval. omnia-splice/src/coordination.ts verifies the proposer signature and enforces an approval decision; the host bypasses both.
findings.impact: A counterparty can submit a correctly formed splice-out that redirects value to an address of its choice, and the host may supply the missing signature automatically.

repro.expected: acceptSplice verifies proposal.proposerSignature and requires an authorised withdrawal/reallocation before signing.
repro.actual: acceptSplice signs the splice digest after parameter checks; the host calls it for any inbound SPLICE_PROPOSAL.
evidence: packages/omnia-splice/src/splice.ts acceptSplice (no proposer signature check / approval)

fix.approach: Move proposer-signature verification and an explicit authorisation callback into the signing boundary. Require a withdrawal/reallocation authorisation when the local entitlement decreases.
constraints: Do not rely on the coordinator for a security property the signer needs.
Verify the proposer signature over the same digest that is signed.
Reject unauthorised economic changes before reserving a leaf.
acceptance: A proposal with an invalid/missing proposer signature is rejected before signing.
A splice-out that reduces the local entitlement requires explicit approval.
Honest proposals still complete.

findings.source: Deeper Omnia host audit, 2026-11-18 (verified against 41106016 / 997b7f4)
findings.title: Factory and VTXO unilateral escape share ports were serialized at scale zero
findings.summary: factoryBalanceStateVariables and poolStateVariables stored share/contribution atoms at state ports 128+k with no MiniNumber scale. The escape scripts use those ports as exact payout amounts, so a 0.2 MINIMA share was read as 2e43 MINIMA and the unilateral exit could not be satisfied. Both builders now emit scale 44, matching coin amounts.
findings.impact: Unilateral escape is the recovery path when counterparties disappear; a fractional share made it unsatisfiable.

repro.expected: Share state serializes with scale 44 so PREVSTATE(128+k) equals the coin amount.
repro.actual: Fixed in both state builders; fractional-scale assertions added.

fix.approach: Apply MINIMA_DECIMALS to every on-chain state port representing a monetary amount, and add fractional KISSVM/escape tests.
constraints: Do not change script wire formats beyond the state scale.
Every value port must share the coin amount scale.
acceptance: Fractional factory shares serialize at scale 44.
Fractional VTXO pool shares serialize at scale 44.

findings.source: Deeper Omnia host audit, 2026-11-18 (verified against 51aed956)
findings.title: A replayed opening proposal could overwrite an established channel
findings.summary: _handleChannelProposal always wrote the reconstructed channel with no existing-channel check, so a counterparty could reset an evolved channel to sequence zero with a different opening split. It now treats an existing channel as authoritative: an exact duplicate (same parties, funding coin/script, token and opening allocation) is an idempotent ACK, and changed opening terms are rejected.
findings.impact: A counterparty could discard the latest jointly signed state and substitute a different opening allocation.

repro.expected: An existing channel is never replaced by a CHANNEL_PROPOSAL.
repro.actual: Fixed: changed opening terms are rejected; identical replays do not overwrite.

fix.approach: Persist the immutable opening allocation and make CHANNEL_PROPOSAL idempotent only for an exact duplicate; all balance changes must use state updates or splice.
constraints: Never reset sequence, latestState or balances from an opening proposal.
acceptance: A changed allocation is rejected.
An identical replay ACKs without overwriting.
The stored channel object is unchanged.

findings.source: Deeper Omnia covenant/transaction audit, 2026-11-18 (verified against 51aed956)
findings.title: Splice transactions encoded atom amounts as whole MINIMA
findings.summary: spliceDraftToMinimaBytes passed atom integers as decimal strings to the core JSON serializer, which encodes an integer string at scale zero. Every splice amount was therefore 10^44 too large. Amounts are now converted with atomsToAmount at the boundary.
findings.impact: Splice-in and splice-out transactions encoded economically incorrect values; agreement between the parties did not detect it.

repro.expected: A 0.2 MINIMA amount round-trips as 0.2, not 2e43.
repro.actual: Fixed: decimal MINIMA is encoded and verified by deserializeTransaction.

fix.approach: Convert atom amounts to canonical decimal strings before the core serializer.
constraints: Never pass an atom integer to a decimal-MINIMA API.
acceptance: Fractional, whole and custom-token amounts round-trip byte-exactly.

findings.source: Deeper Omnia covenant/transaction audit, 2026-11-18 (verified against 51aed956)
findings.title: The splice finalizer constructed a noncanonical witness without spending proofs
findings.summary: assembleSpliceWitness used bespoke 4-byte counts and wrote zero coin/script proofs, unlike serializeOmniaWitness. The finalizer now uses the shared encoder in MULTISIG key order and refuses to broadcast without proofs for every spending input.
findings.impact: A broadcast splice could carry a witness the node cannot validate.

repro.expected: The witness matches the canonical serializer and carries proofs.
repro.actual: Fixed: canonical witness with mandatory proofs before broadcast.

fix.approach: Use the canonical witness encoder and require proof material to broadcast.
constraints: Witness signatures follow MULTISIG key order.
acceptance: Broadcast without proofs is rejected.
A proof-backed splice broadcasts.

findings.source: Deeper Omnia covenant/transaction audit, 2026-11-18 (verified against 51aed956)
findings.title: Factory unilateral exits enforce the original funding shares, not the latest signed factory state
findings.summary: The factory timeout path paid the immutable funding split and authorized the spend with N-of-N signatures without checking the payout set. RFC-079 now implements two complementary settlement branches: per-party escape and an output-enforced full distribution that reads every share from PREVSTATE, pins the output count, destination, amount and total, and needs only one participant signature to trigger. Full distribution is funded by default, and checkpoint enforcement is on by default: the cooperative branch only accepts a checkpoint (same script, same value, sequence + 1), and off-chain allocation changes (virtual-channel open/close, reallocate) are refused until the change is committed as a checkpoint. The escapes therefore read the latest committed allocation, never a stale funding split.
findings.impact: A broadcaster can no longer redirect, resize, drop or add a payout, and a participant can no longer move value off chain (VC open/close, reallocate) and then escape against the old share: those changes are refused until checkpointed. Remaining: the host does not yet submit the checkpoint transaction, so virtual channels are blocked on a checkpointed factory; newer uncommitted off-chain states still require the contest protocol; virtual-channel reserves are not distributable.

repro.expected: Every committed factory transition has an enforceable recovery artifact for its latest allocation.
repro.actual: Redirected, resized, missing, extra and wrong-token payouts are rejected; one participant signature settles a valid distribution; a checkpointed factory refuses VC open/close and reallocate until the allocation change is checkpointed (tests/unit/omnia-factory/src/__tests__/distribution.test.ts, checkpoint.test.ts).

fix.approach: Per RFC-079: (a) output-enforced full distribution plus the per-party escape, both bound to the latest confirmed allocation (checkpoint mode); (b) the pre-signed compact mode is kept as a separate, clearly documented mechanism that does not verify allocations; (c) the contestable recovery protocol remains the target for uncommitted off-chain states.
constraints: A payout set must be derived from PREVSTATE, never from a caller-supplied allocation map.
Do not weaken the output checks to preserve an O(1) instruction claim.
Refuse to distribute while a virtual channel still holds value.
acceptance: A signed virtual-channel payment is enforceable by the losing party on chain.
Escape pays the latest signed allocation, not the original contribution.

findings.source: Deeper Omnia covenant/transaction audit, 2026-11-18 (verified against 51aed956)
findings.title: The default co-signer could authorize HTLC fulfilment without a preimage
findings.summary: validateHtlcSet only compared terms while both versions stayed pending, so a peer could mark an HTLC fulfilled and credit itself while keeping the id. A pending → fulfilled transition now requires a matching preimage, and pending → timed_out requires an authoritative chain height.
findings.impact: A conditional payment could be released without satisfying its hashlock.

repro.expected: Terminal HTLC transitions require proof.
repro.actual: Fixed: preimage/hashlock and chain-height evidence are mandatory.

fix.approach: Validate terminal transitions against the stored record plus the revealed preimage or chain height.
constraints: Never sign a fulfilment without a verified preimage.
acceptance: Fulfilment without a preimage is rejected.
A wrong preimage is rejected.
Timeouts need height.

findings.source: Omnia SDK audit — 25 November 2026, reporter finding OMN-064
findings.title: An LSP open quote is executed without verifying its signature, terms or policy
findings.summary: openQuote() checks only that the quote has not expired and that providerId matches the manifest, then passes the quote straight to the funding host. It does not verify the quote signature, recompute the terms hash from the quoted fields, re-run the admission policy, or bind the quote to the caller. Any caller that can reach this method can therefore present a quote the provider never signed.
findings.impact: If the facade is exposed through an untrusted API, a forged or modified quote can initiate a provider-funded channel on terms the provider never approved. Downstream host limits bound the loss, but the LSP authorization boundary itself is absent, so the provider's commercial policy is advisory.

repro.expected: openQuote() rejects a quote whose signature does not verify over the canonical terms, whose termsHash does not match the quoted fields, or whose terms no longer satisfy the current policy.
repro.actual: A hand-built quote with signature 'x', an inflated remoteAmount and a stale termsHash is passed to host.openChannel and the host is asked to fund it. Only expiresAt and providerId are inspected.
evidence: packages/omnia-lsp-provider/src/provider.ts:140-151 — openQuote checks expiresAt and providerId only
packages/omnia-lsp-provider/src/quote.ts:111-116 — signOpenQuote attaches the signature and nothing consumes it on the way back in
packages/omnia-lsp/src/quote.ts:152-170 — quoteMatchesManifest compares identity fields, not the signature or terms hash

fix.approach: Recompute termsHash from the quoted fields, verify the provider signature over it with the manifest's identity key, require quote.consumerPartyId/consumerPublicKeyDigest to equal the authenticated caller, re-run evaluateOpenRequest against current policy and capacity, and consume the issued quote id atomically before calling the host.
constraints: Do not accept a structurally valid quote as authentic: signature verification is mandatory, not optional.
Structure the API so the unverified path cannot be reached by accident (make raw openQuote internal).
Do not weaken the check for local testing; inject a test signer/clock instead.
acceptance: An unsigned, re-signed-by-another-key, or field-mutated quote is rejected before the host is called.
A quote issued to one consumer cannot be redeemed by another caller.
Replaying an already-consumed quote id is refused.
A quote that no longer satisfies policy is refused even when its signature is valid.

findings.source: Omnia SDK audit — 25 November 2026, reporter finding OMN-065
findings.title: Admission validates the consumer contribution only, then the host swaps the two sides
findings.summary: evaluateOpenRequest() checks minChannel, maxChannel and direction capacity against request.localAmount alone. request.remoteAmount — the provider's own capital commitment — is never compared with the asset limits or available funds. The host adapter then maps quote.remoteAmount to the host's localAmount, so the unvalidated field becomes the provider's actual funding amount.
findings.impact: The provider's real capital commitment is not constrained by the advertised channel limits or capacity policy. A consumer-supplied remoteAmount is the amount the provider funds, so the manifest's maxChannel is bypassable and the provider's exposure is set by its counterparty.

repro.expected: Admission validates both contributions independently, and the total channel value, available provider funds and directional liquidity against the manifest.
repro.actual: Only localAmount is range- and capacity-checked; remoteAmount is unconstrained and is passed to totem_omniaOpenChannel as localAmount (the provider side).

fix.approach: Validate both sides: each contribution against minChannel/maxChannel, the sum against total capacity, the provider side against the asset's outbound/inbound capacity for the requested direction, and against a provider-supplied available-funds bound. Quote both amounts explicitly so the consumer sees what it is asking the provider to commit.
constraints: Do not keep the manifest's limits meaningful for one side only.
Keep the consumer's perspective in the wire quote; perform the swap once, at the host boundary.
Do not infer provider capacity from the host's coin selection.
acceptance: A request whose remoteAmount exceeds maxChannel or provider capacity is refused.
Total channel value is bounded independently of how it is split.
The provider-side amount the host funds equals the amount admission approved.
Directional capacity is checked against the side that actually supplies it.

findings.source: Omnia SDK audit — 25 November 2026, reporter finding OMN-072
findings.title: A splice successor is identified by address, token and amount only, not by lineage from the splice
findings.summary: observeSpliceSuccessor() selects the successor coin by matching address, token id and amount among unspent coins, and excludes spent coins. It does not establish that the coin was created by the intended splice transaction, and it does not explicitly exclude the predecessor funding coin. Rejecting two or more matches does not cover the single-wrong-match case.
findings.impact: A channel can be activated against a coin the splice did not create, or against an incorrect state commitment. The guard against ambiguity is real but narrow: any single unrelated coin with the same address, token and amount is adopted silently.

repro.command: cd artifacts/canary && pnpm run canary run 18-omnia-splice
repro.expected: The successor is accepted only when the splice transaction is on chain, consumed the predecessor, and created this coin with the expected state, sequence and balance commitment.
repro.actual: Observation is a set filter over getCoins(address, tokenId). A coin funded to the same channel address by an unrelated transaction satisfies it.
evidence: CAN-012 records the ambiguity case; the lineage case is still open

fix.approach: Verify transaction lineage before activation: the splice tx must be mined, its first input must be the predecessor coin, and the successor must appear among its outputs with the expected state variables, sequence and total. Then observe burial depth on that coin id.
constraints: Do not rely on a predicted coin id: the channel input floats (COINID_ELTOO).
Do not weaken the multi-match rejection; add lineage on top.
Fail closed when the chain adapter cannot return the spending transaction.
acceptance: A coin with a matching address/token/amount but a different creating transaction is rejected.
The predecessor coin is never accepted as its own successor.
Successor sequence and balance commitment are checked against the accepted splice terms.

findings.title: The watchtower treats a stale-state successor as channel continuity
findings.source: Omnia adversarial audit — 26 November 2026, reporter finding OMN-094 (omnia-host/src/watch.ts:118-145)
findings.summary: The watch service treated any unspent successor coin at the funding address as channel continuity. It did not compare the successor's sequence or state commitment with the latest signed local state, which is exactly the case a watchtower must contest. The contest callback also proved the original funding coin rather than the live successor.
findings.impact: A counterparty publishing an older signed state can settle it unchallenged: the watcher never reports a close, and even if it did, the proof would be for a spent coin. This is the failure mode that makes eltoo watchtowers necessary.

repro.command: cd artifacts/canary && pnpm run canary run 23-chaos-recovery
repro.expected: A successor whose sequence is below the latest signed local state raises a contestable finding and contests the live coin.
repro.actual: Any successor was treated as continuity, and proofs were taken from channel.fundingCoinId.

fix.approach: Read the successor sequence from its state (port 101), compare with latestState.sequence, raise a contestable close when behind, and prove the live coin in the contest path.
constraints: Do not contest normal updates (sequence >= local).
Keep behaviour unchanged when the adapter cannot report a sequence.
acceptance: A stale successor produces a unilateral-close finding naming the live coin.
The contest path proves the observed live coin.
Scans do not overlap.

findings.title: No consensus-enforced channel domain: identical parties and delay share a script
findings.source: Omnia adversarial audit — 26 November 2026, reporter finding OMN-095 (omnia/src/script.ts:43-92, omnia/src/transactions.ts:400-458)
findings.summary: The eltoo funding script is derived from the two public keys and the contest delay, with no unique channel identifier. The update input floats via COINID_ELTOO, and the covenant does not check that the successor's channel identity matches the coin being spent. Multiple channels between the same parties therefore share a script address, and the signed state commitment is not bound by the script.
findings.impact: A signed artifact may be executable in a sibling channel domain. The audit did not demonstrate a replay, but the isolation invariant is absent from the covenant, which is the only place it can be enforced.

repro.expected: Every continuation is bound to an immutable channel domain identifier enforced by the script.
repro.actual: The script pins only settlement (port 100) and sequence (port 101).

fix.approach: Add an immutable channel domain id to the funding script or a dedicated state port that every continuation must preserve; add a regression test on Hawk and the Java node.
constraints: Changing the funding script is a wire change: version it.
Do not rely on an off-chain commitment alone.
acceptance: A signed update from channel A is rejected against channel B with identical parties and delay.
Hawk and Java agree on the rejection.

findings.title: A channel is funded before either party holds a unilateral exit package
findings.source: Omnia adversarial audit — 26 November 2026, reporter finding OMN-096 (omnia/src/channel.ts:167-198, channel.ts:234-325, settlement.ts:417-433)
findings.summary: The opening builder creates the channel with latestState null and sequence 0, then funding is broadcast. startUnilateralClose requires a signed state carrying a valid close package, so during the opening window the funding coin exists on chain with no independent recovery path.
findings.impact: If the counterparty disappears or refuses to co-sign the first state, the capital is stranded behind cooperation. Provider-funded LSP channels carry this exposure for the provider.

repro.expected: Funding broadcast requires an initial, fully signed state with a verified close package.
repro.actual: latestState is null at funding; the close package arrives only after a cooperative update.

fix.approach: Make a signed sequence-0 state with a verified close package a precondition of the funding broadcast, and persist it before broadcasting.
constraints: Do not weaken the close-package verification.
Keep the proposal flow usable: the initial state can travel with the proposal.
acceptance: A funding broadcast without a persisted close package is refused.
A restart after funding can always start a unilateral close.

findings.title: VTXO epoch admission has a check-then-sign race
findings.source: Omnia adversarial audit — 26 November 2026, reporter finding OMN-104 (vtxo/src/epoch-authority.ts:111-153)
findings.summary: append() verifies the receipt, loads state, checks spent inputs, signs the epoch commitment and appends. The checks and the signing are separated by awaits with no reservation, so two concurrent appends can both pass the spent-input check and sign conflicting spends or roots.
findings.impact: The epoch authority is the durable single-spend guard for receipts; admitting two conflicting transitions makes it ineffective.

repro.expected: Inputs and the epoch transition are reserved atomically before a signature is produced.
repro.actual: Checks and signing are separate steps.

fix.approach: Reserve inputs and the epoch transition with a revision-checked durable transaction before signing; conflicting requests fail before the signature.
constraints: Do not sign before the reservation commits.
Keep the journal append idempotent per receipt id.
acceptance: Two concurrent receipts spending the same input admit one.
No signature exists for a rejected transition.

findings.title: Signing admission reads an unreadable journal as "no history"
findings.source: Omnia adversarial audit — 26 November 2026, reporter finding OMN-106 (omnia/src/guards.ts:217-249)
findings.summary: beginSigningAttempt caught every journal read error and continued with an empty history, then recorded the intent and allowed signing. The journal also defaulted to an in-memory implementation, so durability existed only if the host installed one. Read, conflict check and write were separate operations.
findings.impact: A storage fault licenses a second WOTS signature at a sequence that may already be signed — leaf reuse. This undermines OMN-039.

repro.expected: An unavailable journal refuses the signature; admission is serialised; the host refuses to run on an in-memory journal without warning.
repro.actual: Read errors were swallowed and admission was unsynchronised.

fix.approach: Fail closed on read and write errors, serialise admission per channel, expose whether the journal is in-memory and warn at host startup.
constraints: Do not weaken double-sign detection.
Keep retries of the same payload idempotent.
acceptance: An unreadable journal refuses signing.
Concurrent different payloads at one sequence admit one.
A host warns when only the memory journal is installed.

origin.note: reporter id OMN-106; The audit is right that OMN-039 was incompletely closed: the durable journal was opt-in.

findings.title: A liquidity position can become active without funding evidence
findings.source: Omnia adversarial audit — 26 November 2026, reporter finding OMN-108 (liquidity-bond/src/position.ts:11-63)
findings.summary: createLiquidityPosition sets status to committed when funding exists and active when it does not, and falls back to the self-declared commitment amount when funding is not chain-confirmed. The exported activation helper rejects non-confirmed funding but permits absent funding. depositToPool verifies on chain; the underlying functions do not.
findings.impact: A position with no backing can be active, allocatable and withdrawable through a path that bypasses depositToPool.

repro.expected: No position becomes active, allocatable or withdrawable without authoritative funding evidence.
repro.actual: status: funding ? committed : active.

fix.approach: Require chain-confirmed funding for active/allocatable status at the position and registry layer, not only in depositToPool.
constraints: Do not break the deposit path.
Keep unfunded records representable as non-active.
acceptance: An unfunded position cannot be listed as withdrawable.
The amount always comes from verified funding.

findings.title: One accepted commitment can create multiple liquidity positions
findings.source: Omnia adversarial audit — 26 November 2026, reporter finding OMN-109 (omnia-pool/src/deposit.ts:152-183, liquidity-bond/src/position.ts:9-46)
findings.summary: createPositionFromCommitment mints a new position id on every call and does not check the registry for an existing position derived from the same commitment. The registry prevents one funding coin backing several commitments, but not one commitment backing several positions.
findings.impact: Recorded liabilities can exceed real backing capital by a multiple of the number of retries.

repro.expected: A commitment produces exactly one position; a retry returns the existing one.
repro.actual: Each call creates a new position id.

fix.approach: Make commitmentId a unique key for position creation and return the existing position on retry.
constraints: Do not allow two positions per commitment.
Keep partial withdrawal receipts separate from positions.
acceptance: Replaying an accepted deposit returns the original position.
The registry rejects a second position for one commitment.

findings.title: Channel funding draft silently drops the unspent part of the funding coin
findings.source: artifacts/canary/src/composition/__tests__/CrossPackage.test.ts
findings.summary: buildFundingTx takes explicit input amounts but always emits exactly one output (the channel coin). It neither returns change nor checks that inputs cover outputs, and buildChannelOpening passes the whole funding coin. Opening a channel from a coin larger than localAmount + remoteAmount therefore produces a draft whose inputs exceed its outputs by the unspent remainder. tx-builder buildTransaction does not check conservation either, so nothing fails until a node rejects the unbalanced transaction.
findings.impact: Reachable from the RPC surface: omnia-host forwards fundingCoinId unchanged, so any wallet that does not pre-select an exactly-sized coin fails to open a channel with an opaque node rejection. No funds are lost (the node refuses the transaction) but the failure is late and misattributed.

repro.expected: The draft either pays the remainder back to the funding coin address (change output) or throws when sum(inputs) > totalValue.
repro.actual: The draft contains a single output. inputs sum 1500 while outputs sum 1000, and no layer rejects it. Recorded as a node:test TODO so it stays visible without failing the gate.
evidence: CANARY FINDING: an over-funded funding draft is neither changed nor rejected (TODO)
packages/omnia/src/channel.ts: buildChannelOpening passes fundingCoin.amount as the input
packages/tx-builder/src/build.ts: buildTransaction has no conservation check

fix.approach: Add a change output to the input coin address in buildFundingTx when sum(inputs) > totalValue, or reject the draft with a clear error. Do both at the right layers: omnia owns channel funding semantics, tx-builder should refuse to serialise an unbalanced transaction rather than deferring to the node.
constraints: Do not change the funding output state contract: STATE(100)=false, STATE(101)=0.
Do not change computeOmniaTxDigest / canonical byte semantics.
Do not mask this in the canary, in omnia-host, or with a coin pre-selection workaround.
Keep the single-input fast path byte-identical when the input equals totalValue.
acceptance: buildFundingTx returns a change output to the funding coin address when inputs exceed totalValue.
buildFundingTx (or buildChannelOpening) throws when inputs are less than totalValue.
tx-builder buildTransaction rejects a draft whose input sum is below its output sum.
Unit tests cover over-funded, exact, and under-funded inputs.
The canary test "over-funded funding draft is neither changed nor rejected" is un-TODOed and passes.

findings.title: Manifest proofs are not bound to the manifest they attest
findings.source: artifacts/canary/src/composition/__tests__/ProofAndMoney.test.ts
findings.summary: verifyManifestProof verifies the manifest signature and the proof envelope independently and never compares them. A proof whose payload.manifestId names a different manifest, a proof of a different kind (attestation), and a proof issued by an unrelated key all verify as valid against any correctly signed manifest.
findings.impact: An attestation issued for one manifest can be presented as attestation for another (for example a later version with the same appId), and a non-manifest proof can be passed off as a manifest attestation. Verifiers that rely on the pairing will over-report assurance.

repro.expected: A proof for manifest A is rejected against manifest B, a non-manifest proof is rejected, and a foreign issuer is rejected.
repro.actual: All three return valid: true, because verifyManifestProof never reads proof.payload, proof.kind or the proof issuer relative to the manifest.
evidence: createManifestProof stores payload { manifestId } from the caller, and nothing compares it back
canary observed: proof for A vs manifest B -> valid; attestation proof vs manifest A -> valid; proof with unrelated manifestId -> valid; proof from a third-party issuer -> valid

fix.approach: Bind the pair explicitly: require proof.kind === 'manifest', require the proof issuer to be the manifest author address, and compare payload.manifestId with the identifier computed from the supplied manifest. Decide and document which identifier that is (content digest via computeManifestId is the strongest; appId is weaker and would still allow version substitution), then make createManifestProof derive it from the SignedManifest rather than trusting a caller string.
constraints: Do not change the manifest signing format or computeManifestId semantics.
Do not accept a wildcard or "any" manifestId to preserve callers.
Keep verifyManifest false-paths and reasons unchanged.
acceptance: verifyManifestProof rejects a proof issued for a different manifest (version substitution).
verifyManifestProof rejects a proof whose kind is not manifest.
verifyManifestProof rejects a proof whose issuer does not match the manifest author.
The honest proof/manifest pair still verifies.
The canary TODO test flips to a normal passing test.

findings.title: Non-custodial channel open races the chain: the acceptor validates the funding coin before it can be mined
findings.source: live runs: omnia-open-noncustodial.mjs against Hawk v0.2.12 and v0.3.0 (us-east-1 hosts A/B)
findings.summary: SubmitOpenChannel posts the funding transaction and, in the same call, sends CHANNEL_PROPOSAL to the counterparty. The responder's acceptChannel requires the funding coin to already exist on chain and throws "Funding coin <id> not found on chain". On a real node the transaction cannot be included in a block in the microseconds between the post and the proposal, so a first-time open always fails. The initiator does not wait for inclusion, and the responder does not wait or retry.
findings.impact: Every two-party channel open against a live node fails at the peer handshake, even though the funding transaction is valid and is mined moments later. Offline and in-memory suites do not catch it because their chain view already contains the coin when the proposal is handled. This blocks every channel-based use case from being opened on a real network.

repro.expected: The responder accepts the proposal and reports status "active" for the channel.
repro.actual: Submit returns success with acknowledged=false; the responder answers CHANNEL_PROPOSAL with ERROR "acceptChannel failed: Error: Funding coin <id> not found on chain"; the status poll on the responder never finds the channel.
evidence: live invocation: NODE=http://127.0.0.1:9005 HOST_B=http://172.31.74.14:50056/rpc WALLET=http://127.0.0.1:51060 FUNDING_COIN_ID=<confirmed 2e8 coin> REMOTE_TRANSPORT=<b transport> LOCAL_AMOUNT=60000000 REMOTE_AMOUNT=40000000 node scripts/omnia-open-noncustodial.mjs
funding tx 0x00012CD06D63AF0F7ED60A4915381BF30D0E8A4FB93647951CC79C9A2DCC1A60 has outputs[0] = that exact coin, 100000000, in block 8
rejection was raised at 12:23:49Z, before block 8 existed on the node
enabling node automine before the run does not help: the check still happens before the post is processed

reproduced unchanged on Hawk v0.3.0 (built from release/0.3.0 @985b859, LMDB+DuckDB): channel 0xe6863650602f6f7a3e1b99df1ebba8d1 rejected coin 0x823afc4cabe74c109c2b1b794d16aec2e0a2362b4b5816d209d62d701065a6d0
packages/omnia/src/channel.ts: acceptChannel resolves the funding coin from the chain provider and throws when absent

fix.approach: Make the handshake tolerate the inclusion delay instead of assuming it away. On the initiator, wait for the funding coin to be observable through the chain provider (bounded, with a named timeout) before sending CHANNEL_PROPOSAL; on the responder, treat "coin not yet found" as retryable for a bounded window rather than an immediate terminal rejection. Either side alone fixes the common case; doing both covers a slow block and a fast initiator.
constraints: Do not remove the on-chain funding-coin check: it is what stops an unfunded channel from being accepted.
Do not raise the existing 20s peer-reply timeout as the mechanism; the wait belongs around chain inclusion.
Do not add an unbounded wait or a sleep-and-hope; bound it and fail with the observed height and coin id.
acceptance: A open against a live node succeeds when the funding tx is mined a few seconds after submission.
An open whose funding tx is never mined fails within a bounded time with a message naming the coin and the chain height.
The responder still rejects a proposal whose funding coin does not exist (no regression in the safety check).
Offline and in-memory suites still pass.
