findings.title: Forwarder signs the outgoing HTLC before the link is durable
findings.source: security audit OMN-NEW-002, verified against source at 8fa26907
findings.summary: forwardIncoming calls addHTLC (which reserves WOTS keys and signs the new state), writes the updated channel into the channel map, builds the link record, and only then calls linkJournal.record(). A crash or a storage failure between the signed state and the journal write leaves an outgoing obligation with no durable incoming-to-outgoing association.
findings.impact: Stranded liquidity and broken backward settlement after a restart: the relay knows it signed an outgoing HTLC on-chain-ish state but cannot reconstruct which incoming HTLC it was forwarding. Contradicts the durability claim the recovery design rests on.

repro.expected: The association is durable before or atomically with the signed outgoing state, so recovery can always pair an outgoing HTLC with its incoming one.
repro.actual: record() runs after addHTLC() and after channels.set(); a failure in between is unrecoverable.
evidence: fix proposed in PR #218 (intent journaled before signing; recovery completes or drops it)

fix.approach: Write an intent record before signing (hashlock, incoming ids, planned outgoing channel/amount/timeout), then sign, then commit the outgoing htlc id. Recovery resolves intents: if the outgoing htlc exists, complete the link; if not, the intent is safe to drop.
constraints: Do not claim durability for a link that was not written before the signature.
Do not make the journal the authority for channel balances.
acceptance: A crash injected between signing and commit leaves a recoverable record.
recover() can reconstruct the link from the intent plus channel state.
Normal forwarding writes the same number of journal entries.

findings.title: Relay recovery discards a link when either side is terminal
findings.source: security audit OMN-NEW-003, verified against source at 8fa26907
findings.summary: recover() keeps a link only while both HTLCs are pending: terminal(inHtlc) || terminal(outHtlc) causes it to delete the link and remove it from the journal. An outgoing HTLC being fulfilled does not imply the incoming one was fulfilled — settling backwards is a separate later step — so the association is dropped at exactly the point it is still needed.
findings.impact: After a restart in the middle of a forward, the link needed to reveal the preimage to the incoming channel is gone. Liquidity on the incoming side stays locked until timeout, and the relay cannot prove the pairing.

repro.expected: A link is discarded only once the incoming HTLC is settled or the pair is provably unspendable.
repro.actual: terminal(outHtlc) alone deletes the link and its journal entry.
evidence: fix proposed in PR #218 (recovery keys on the incoming HTLC only)

fix.approach: Split the terminal condition: an outgoing HTLC that is fulfilled means "reveal the preimage to the incoming side", not "done". Discard only when the incoming HTLC is settled or both sides are timed out.
constraints: Do not keep links forever: unresolved links must have a timeout-based exit.
Do not reveal a preimage without the corresponding fulfilled outgoing HTLC.
acceptance: recover() returns links whose outgoing HTLC is fulfilled and whose incoming HTLC is still pending.
Those links settle backwards after recovery.
A link whose incoming HTLC is settled is still removed.

findings.title: Both live splice paths omit chainProvider, so a broadcast splice is marked active with a placeholder coin
findings.source: security audit OMN-NEW-005, verified against source at 8fa26907
findings.summary: observeSpliceSuccessor exists precisely because the predecessor coin is spent and the successor must be found on chain. finalizeSplice only calls it when options.chainProvider is set; otherwise it defaults successorStatus to "active" and spliceFundingCoinId to `${txid}-0`, which is a placeholder. Both host call sites (prepared splice and direct splice) pass no chainProvider.
findings.impact: A splice is treated as confirmed before its successor coin exists. The channel is reported active with a coin id that is not a real output, restart recovery has nothing valid to resume from, and later operations can act on a channel that the chain does not have.

repro.expected: A spliced channel stays funding_pending until the successor coin is observed on chain.
repro.actual: Without chainProvider the branch is skipped and status is set to active immediately.
evidence: fix proposed in PR #218 (finalizeSplice defaults to funding_pending; both call sites pass a chain observer)
packages/omnia-splice/src/finalize.ts:345 — let successorStatus = "active"; only replaced inside if (options?.chainProvider)

fix.approach: Pass the host chain adapter at both call sites, and make the absence of a chainProvider an error rather than an implicit "assume active". Default to funding_pending when observation is unavailable.
constraints: Do not use `${txid}-0` as a funding coin id for any state that can be acted on.
Do not block the RPC indefinitely: observation stays bounded.
acceptance: Both call sites pass a chain provider.
finalizeSplice without observation yields funding_pending, never active.
A splice becomes active only after the successor is found with the required confirmations.

findings.title: withChannelLock only guards the direct pay path
findings.source: security audit OMN-NEW-007, verified against source at 8fa26907
findings.summary: withChannelLock is defined once and used exactly once, around the direct omniaPay RPC. HTLC operations, prepared submissions, settlement and splice paths do not take it, so they can read, modify and write the same channel concurrently.
findings.impact: Concurrent RPC or peer-driven operations can interleave read-modify-write cycles. The signing watermark blocks some conflicting signatures but does not serialize state derivation, so a lost update or a state built on a stale sequence is possible.

repro.expected: Every channel mutation, whatever its entry point, runs under one per-channel coordinator.
repro.actual: One use of withChannelLock, in the direct pay handler.
evidence: fix proposed in PR #218 (shared re-entrant per-channel lock across RPC and peer handlers)

fix.approach: Move the lock into the channel store or a mutation coordinator and take it in every path that mutates a channel: pay, HTLC add/reveal/timeout, prepared submit, settlement and splice, including peer handlers.
constraints: Do not rely on the watermark as the serialization mechanism.
Do not introduce a global lock that serializes unrelated channels.
acceptance: All mutation entry points acquire the same per-channel lock.
A concurrency test that interleaves two mutations yields a consistent sequence with no lost update.

findings.title: The watchtower is implemented and exported but never started by the host
findings.source: security audit OMN-NEW-008, verified against source at 8fa26907
findings.summary: createChannelWatchService exists with detection and retry logic and is exported from the package index, but no code calls it: createOmniaHost().start() contains no reference to it. Its close detection also keys on the original funding coin being spent, which cannot distinguish a unilateral close from an update or splice, and it adds the channel to a persistent closed set.
findings.impact: A host holding funds runs with no automated response to a unilateral close: no contest transaction is produced before the deadline. Where the service is used manually, a normal update can be misread as a close and suppress later events.

repro.expected: The host starts a chain-aware watcher that tracks successive channel coins and deadlines.
repro.actual: Only the definition and the export exist; lifecycle.ts has no watcher.
evidence: fix proposed in PR #218 (watch service started by the host; successor-aware close detection)
packages/omnia-host/src/lifecycle.ts — no reference to the watch service

fix.approach: Start the watcher in host.start() and stop it in close(). Track the current channel coin per sequence rather than the original funding coin, distinguish update from close by the spending transaction, and handle reorgs and contest deadlines.
constraints: Do not treat "funding coin spent" as equivalent to "unilateral close".
Do not let the persistent closed set suppress later events for a channel that is still live.
acceptance: Host startup starts the watcher and shutdown stops it.
A simulated unilateral close triggers the contest path before the deadline.
A normal state update or splice does not mark the channel closed.

findings.title: Finalization guards validate identifiers, not the resulting state
findings.source: re-audit R-002, verified against source at 5d8c427b
findings.summary: CAN-007 stopped unsolicited finalizations by requiring a local acceptance. But assertSpliceFinalized checks ids (spliceId, channelId, splicedFrom, txId) and assertVcFinalized checks kind, factory and a one-step sequence. Neither compares balances, totalValue or allocations with the locally signed proposal. Separately, FACTORY_CLOSE_FINALIZED marks a known factory closed with no settlement check.
findings.impact: A counterparty can finalize a transition whose economic terms differ from what was accepted, as long as the identifiers line up. A factory can be marked closed without proof that settlement happened.

repro.expected: The finalized channel/factory is compared field-by-field with the accepted proposal, including balances, totalValue and allocations, and signatures over that state verify.
repro.actual: Only identifiers and the sequence step are compared.
evidence: packages/omnia-host/src/peer-guards.ts — assertSpliceFinalized compares ids and txId only
packages/omnia-host/src/peer-guards.ts — assertVcFinalized compares factoryId and sequence only
packages/omnia-host/src/lifecycle.ts:459-462 — FACTORY_CLOSE_FINALIZED sets status closed without settlement evidence

fix.approach: Pass the locally accepted proposal/acceptance into the guards and compare the complete finalized state (balances, totalValue, allocations, virtual-channel set) plus the signatures over it. Require settlement evidence before a factory is marked closed.
constraints: Do not weaken the existing id checks.
Do not accept a finalized state that differs in any economically meaningful field.
acceptance: A finalized splice with altered balances is rejected.
A VC finalization whose allocations differ from the signed plan is rejected.
FACTORY_CLOSE_FINALIZED without settlement evidence does not close the factory.

findings.title: Factory opening requests the funding signature before the proposal exists (regression from CAN-010)
findings.source: re-audit R-003, verified against source at 5d8c427b
findings.summary: prepareFactory builds the plan and immediately sends FACTORY_FUNDING_REQUEST; FACTORY_PROPOSAL is only sent later by submitFactory (and by createFactoryMethod after its own signer call). CAN-010 now requires the receiver to hold an accepted factory with a matching pendingCommitment before it will sign, which cannot be true yet. The two changes contradict each other, so a fresh two-host factory opening fails at the funding step.
findings.impact: Factory opening is blocked on the prepared path and likely on the createFactory path. This is a functional regression introduced by the CAN-010 fix, not a pre-existing defect.

repro.expected: prepare → sign → finalize completes against a second host.
repro.actual: The responder answers ERROR ("does not match any locally accepted factory") because it has not received the proposal yet.
evidence: fix proposed in PR #222: both host paths send FACTORY_PROPOSAL first and use the acceptance as the funding witness
packages/omnia-host/src/api/methods.ts:2752 — createFactory method requests the signature before its proposal too

fix.approach: Reorder both flows so the proposal (with funding materials) establishes the pending factory before any funding signature is requested, and use the responder opening signature over the same commitment as the funding witness instead of a second round. Add a FACTORY_FINALIZED follow-up so the responder learns the funding txid after the proposer broadcasts.
constraints: Do not relax CAN-010 back into an unbound signing oracle.
Do not allow a second FACTORY_PROPOSAL to re-sign after acceptance.
acceptance: A two-host prepare → sign → finalize run completes and both sides hold the same funding txid.
An unsigned/unknown digest is still refused.

findings.title: Hawk 0.3.0 cannot complete mainnet IBD: block proofs rejected, blocks skipped, tip parks ~1,000 behind
findings.source: live run 15 Nov 2026: mainnet node on host A (us-east-1), 0.3.0 vs 0.2.12
findings.summary: A fresh Hawk 0.3.0 node on mainnet (no -test, no -solo) syncs to block 2,418,985 and then loops on "Invalid MMR Proof! @ 2418985", never advancing and never binding the RPC port. The 0.2.12 release, started on the same host minutes later, completed IBD to block 2,421,050 via cascade with zero MMR errors.
findings.impact: The canary gate requires Hawk 0.3.0 (exact match), so no live scenario can run against the current build on mainnet. Factory, channel and settlement evidence cannot be produced until 0.3.0 syncs or the gate is given a documented exception.

repro.expected: The node reaches /readyz 200 on mainnet and the run proceeds.
repro.actual: readyz stays 000; the log repeats "Invalid MMR Proof! @ 2418985" for the same block indefinitely.
evidence: root cause 4 (residual 171->998 MMR lines at the tip): checkMMR validated a block's own witness proofs against the parent MMR. Blocks that carry their own coin set (superblocks) can never match it; the block's coin set is bound by its own MMR root, which checkTxPoWBlock/blockStateMatches rebuild and compare. Skipping the per-proof check for blocks (transactions stay strict) gives 0 MMR lines in 150s while the chain advanced 6 blocks, versus ~3/min before

root cause 3 found: checkTxBlockOnly compares the block difficulty against a trailing average over the local tree, which cannot match for a historical IBD block. Block 2420149 failed with "Incorrect TxPoW block difficulty" and everything after was skipped for a missing parent
with all three fixes the same build synced from scratch on mainnet to block 2421363 against a peer top of 2421362, syncing 0, zero difficulty rejections (171 residual MMR lines, non-blocking)
experiments rejected: reverting tx_pow_tree to 0.2.12 (sort order + side-branch collection) still parks at 2420225 and raises MMR errors to 754; setSyncIBD call sites are identical in both versions
residual is in IBD peer/response selection: the node loops asking a peer whose batch top (2420114) is below its own tip (2420148) and discards the blocks as historical; IBD_LIMIT_MINS is new in 0.3.0

root cause 2 found: the one-greeting-per-connection guard (new in 0.3.0) returns early on the duplicate, suppressing the IBD retry that 0.2.12 used to obtain its cascade. With the guard relaxed a fresh node logged Cascade: Loading 3361 nodes within a minute and reached the cascade tip with 0 MMR errors

both fixes are on minima-more PR #2; residual: after adopting the cascade the node sits at the cascade tip and loops requesting IBD at tip-1, receiving batches that end below its tip and are ignored as historical
after threading the offset through checkTxPoWSimple for transactions inside a block: still parks, this time at 2420143 with 411 MMR errors, readyz 200, syncing 0, ~1090 blocks behind the peer
hundreds of "SyncBlock missing parent (skipping, not fatal)" lines: the tree is rebuilt from a subset, so the batch top is never reached and the IBD loop finishes early

with the block-proof offset fix (minima-more PR #2): 0 Invalid MMR Proof, RPC binds, but the node then stalls at "No TxPoWTree yet.. required for NIO_SYNCTXBLOCK" and never receives a cascade; readyz stays 503 after 13 minutes
0.2.12 on the same host logs "Cascade: Loading 3361 nodes" and reaches block 2421050
0.3.0: peer ahead top=2421118, IBD requested, tip stuck at 2418985, RPC never bound
0.3.0 log: 200+ lines of "Invalid MMR Proof! @ 2418985", tip unchanged for >3 minutes
0.2.12 on the same host: readyz 200, block 2421050, syncing 0, 0 MMR errors, ~2 min via cascade

witnessesMatch (blockStateMatches) verifies coin proofs with parentMMR.checkProof because block proofs are one block ahead, but the sync path calls checkTxBlockOnly/checkTxPoWSimple first, which use checkProofTimeValid against the parent MMR

fix.approach: Make the sync-block path use the same one-block-ahead proof semantics that blockStateMatches already uses, for the block TxPoW and any local transaction bodies, instead of checkProofTimeValid against the parent MMR. Then re-run mainnet IBD on a clean data dir and require the tip to track the peer.
constraints: Do not disable the witness gate by default to hide this: IBD_WITNESS_CHECK is already false.
Do not weaken blockStateMatches while fixing the earlier check.
acceptance: A fresh 0.3.x node on mainnet reaches readyz 200 and tracks the peer tip across a cascade boundary.
No "Invalid MMR Proof" loop at any height.
verification: hawk-node: start on mainnet with a clean data dir and watch /readyz and the tip

findings.title: Liquidity-bond passes an atom count as the verifier's decimal claimedAmount, rejecting every pool deposit
findings.source: omnia-host pool test against the real deposit path (`depositToPool` -> `verifyDeposit`)
findings.summary: `VerifyDepositParams.claimedAmount` is decimal MINIMA text (chain-provider compares it with the node's decimal `coin.amount`). liquidity-bond built it from `commitment.amount.toString()`, and `commitment.amount` is an atom count, so the omnia-host verifier converted it to atoms a second time. A 100000 MINIMA deposit became 1e93 atoms at the comparison.
findings.impact: Every non-zero liquidity-pool deposit failed the amount gate with "insufficient amount", and `acceptLiquidityCommitment`/`confirmLiquidityCommitment` refused to accept or confirm funding. The failure looked like a funding problem, not a unit bug.

repro.expected: a commitment for a funded coin of 100000 MINIMA passes on-chain verification.
repro.actual: `insufficient amount`: coinAmountAtoms(coin) = 1e49 vs amountToAtoms("1" + 49 zeros) = 1e93.

fix.approach: Render the commitment amount as decimal text at the verifier boundary with `atomsToAmount(commitment.amount)`; keep the verifier contract decimal and the internal ledger in atoms.
constraints: Do not change `VerifyDepositParams.claimedAmount` to atoms; it compares against the node's decimal `coin.amount`.
Do not weaken the amount gate.
acceptance: A 100000 MINIMA pool deposit verifies and is accepted.
An under-funded coin still fails.
The omnia-host pool lifecycle test passes unchanged in assertions.

findings.title: mintVtxo replaces the pool commitment root with a single-leaf tree
findings.source: Omnia whole-family re-audit (2026-11-17), finding OMN-002
findings.summary: mintVtxo builds its proof set from `[vtxo]` and assigns that single-leaf root to `pool.commitmentRoot`. The pool type holds no membership set and the mint does not advance epoch or batchId, so a second mint replaces the root and the first VTXO no longer verifies against the pool.
findings.impact: Previously minted claims stop verifying against the pool root. Any verifier that anchors on the current root rejects legitimate holders; there is no epoch history to fall back to.

repro.expected: After minting A then B, A and B both verify against the pool root the operator publishes.
repro.actual: pool.commitmentRoot equals the root of B alone; A's proof points at the earlier root.
evidence: packages/omnia-vtxo/src/types.ts: OmniaVtxoPool has commitmentRoot but no membership set

fix.approach: Decide the contract first: either commitmentRoot covers the whole active set (the pool carries the member leaves and mint rebuilds the tree) or it covers one epoch (mint advances epoch/batchId and the epoch journal is the authority for historical proofs). Implement the chosen contract atomically and record it in docs.
constraints: Do not silently keep the single-leaf root — it makes the field mean something different from its name.
Existing VTXO ids and leaves must not change.
Epoch roots must remain verifiable after later mints.
acceptance: Two sequential mints leave both proofs verifiable against the published root.
The pool type can represent the membership set or explicitly states per-epoch scope.
A regression test mints N VTXOs and verifies all N.

findings.title: Pool payout settlement is an unverified caller assertion
findings.source: Omnia whole-family re-audit (2026-11-17), finding OMN-004
findings.summary: executePoolPayout correctly refuses to settle without evidence, but when `settlement` is supplied it stores it, marks the intent settled-externally, decrements capital and consumes the receipt without checking the evidence. The host casts the RPC parameter to the same type.
findings.impact: A caller with pool-management access can advance accounting as if a payout happened. Whether that is theft depends on who can reach the RPC, but the accounting no longer reflects chain or channel reality.

repro.expected: A settlement object that does not reference the withdrawal id, amount, recipient and pool is rejected and leaves the registry unchanged.
repro.actual: Any object is stored; the intention is marked settled and the receipt consumed.

fix.approach: Verify finality before mutating: for `confirmed` check the transaction against the chain provider and the required depth; for `offchain-final` verify a signed settlement from the channel/factory. Bind the evidence to the exact withdrawal id, amount, recipient and pool.
constraints: No unconditional settlement path, including through the host RPC.
Do not accept a bare boolean or opaque object as finality.
Keep the prepared-draft path unchanged for callers without evidence.
acceptance: Forged or mismatched settlement evidence leaves the registry byte-identical.
A settlement for another withdrawal id, amount, recipient or pool is rejected.
The valid confirmed and offchain-final paths still settle.

findings.title: recordPoolFee trusts a caller-supplied `verified` flag
findings.source: Omnia whole-family re-audit (2026-11-17), finding OMN-005
findings.summary: recordPoolFee forwards `params.verified` into recordLiquidityFee, where earnable records count toward LP entitlement only when `verified === true`. The verifier exists (`feeProofVerifier.verifyFeeProof`) but this path never calls it. claimFees and compoundFees likewise accept any `payoutRef` without confirming it is a settled payout.
findings.impact: A caller trusted to record fees can manufacture verified earnings, or compound them into principal, without establishing that any fee was paid.

repro.expected: An earnable fee record without a verifiable proof cannot increase unclaimed LP fees.
repro.actual: `verified: true` is accepted as-is and the record becomes earnable.
evidence: packages/liquidity-bond/src/fees.ts: the verifier is only used by the separate proof path

fix.approach: Replace the boolean with a verification capability: recordPoolFee either receives a verifier and proof, or records the fee as unverified. Claims and compounds must consume a unique settled payout reference.
constraints: No caller-controlled boolean may gate earnable accounting.
Keep unverified records visible for audit but non-earnable.
Reused payout references must be rejected, not ignored.
acceptance: A forged `verified` flag cannot increase unclaimed fees.
A claim or compound with an unknown or reused payoutRef is rejected.
The verified path still credits the LP.

findings.title: Multi-hop recovery does not journal the outstanding backward preimage duty
findings.source: Omnia whole-family re-audit (2026-11-17), finding OMN-006
findings.summary: revealPreimage fulfils the incoming HTLC (changing signed state) before sending the update to the previous hop. If the send fails, the journal survives — but recover() clears any link whose incoming HTLC is no longer pending, which is now true, so the duty to propagate the preimage backwards is lost. Separately, the host multi-hop RPC throws on failure and discards the router's structured `pendingRefunds`.
findings.impact: Reopened by the deeper audit: the final-recipient branch of forwardIncoming still fulfils the incoming HTLC and sends the preimage upstream without first journaling the delivery obligation, so a crash between fulfil and send is unrecoverable. A payment can be settled on the outgoing side and never settled backwards, leaving liquidity locked and the payer's HTLC stuck until timeout. Refund obligations are not reported to the caller.

repro.expected: After a failed backward send, restart recovery still knows the preimage must be delivered to the previous hop.
repro.actual: The journal entry is removed because the incoming HTLC is terminal, and the preimage is never retried.
evidence: packages/omnia-relay/src/forwarder.ts: fulfilHTLC then sendMessage then journal.remove
packages/omnia-relay/src/forwarder.ts: recover() clears terminal incoming links

fix.approach: Journal distinct states (forward-intent, outgoing-signed, outgoing-accepted, preimage-received, backward-sent, peer-acked, complete) and replay them idempotently on restart. Return pending refunds to the caller on failure instead of dropping them.
constraints: Do not clear a link until the backward settlement is acknowledged or provably terminal.
Replay must be idempotent: no double settlement on repeated recovery.
Keep the journal the single authority; do not infer from channel state alone.
acceptance: A crash after fulfilHTLC but before send leaves recoverable state that retries the backward send.
Repeated recovery never settles the same HTLC twice.
A failed multi-hop call surfaces pendingRefunds to the RPC caller.

origin.note: Partially aliased: the dropped pendingRefunds overlap CAN-022 and the relay journal halves overlap CAN-008/CAN-009. The new part is the durable backward-preimage duty after fulfilHTLC.

findings.title: VTXO claim verification accepts a caller-supplied signer list
findings.source: Omnia whole-family re-audit (2026-11-17), finding OMN-007
findings.summary: The claim policy evaluates membership in `witness.signers: string[]`, which is a list of names, not signatures. The host exposes `omnia/verifyVtxoClaim` and passes `params.signers`, the caller-chosen block height and HTLC status straight through, returning `success: true`.
findings.impact: Any caller can obtain a "valid" claim result by asserting the right names and block. If an operator or integration treats that result as authorisation, a VTXO can be claimed without a signature.

repro.expected: Claim verification requires signatures over the canonical claim preimage and rejects a name list.
repro.actual: `{signers: ["beneficiary"], block: <cliff>}` returns valid without any signature check.

fix.approach: Split the policy evaluator from verification. The host must verify signatures over the claim preimage before calling the policy, and take the block from the chain provider rather than the request. Rename the RPC result so it cannot be read as an authorisation.
constraints: Do not accept a signer name list as evidence of a signature.
The block height must come from chain state for the authoritative path.
Keep the pure policy function usable for offline evaluation.
acceptance: A claim with no signature or a wrong signer signature is rejected by the host.
A caller-supplied block that is ahead of the chain tip is ignored or rejected.
The valid signed claim path still succeeds.

findings.title: verifyVtxo accepts a VTXO with no membership proof and never anchors the root
findings.source: Omnia whole-family re-audit (2026-11-17), finding OMN-010
findings.summary: verifyVtxo only checks the proof when `proof.leaf` and `proof.root` are present, and verifyVtxoProof checks the tree against the root carried in the proof itself. Nothing compares that root to the pool's anchored root, and the function never receives the pool.
findings.impact: A VTXO with no proof, or with a self-consistent proof against a root the operator never published, can be reported valid. Combined with OMN-002 there is no current root to anchor against.

repro.expected: A VTXO whose proof root is not the anchored pool root is invalid.
repro.actual: The proof is skipped when absent; when present it is checked only against its own root.

fix.approach: Take the expected root as a required argument (or a pool/epoch record) and fail closed when the proof is missing or points elsewhere. Keep a separate structural check for offline inspection.
constraints: Missing proof must be an error on the authoritative path, not a skipped check.
Do not silently trust a root supplied by the artifact under test.
acceptance: A VTXO without a proof fails authoritative verification.
A proof against a different root fails.
A valid proof against the anchored root passes.

findings.title: Splice recovery can attach one observed successor to several pending splices
findings.source: Omnia whole-family re-audit (2026-11-17), finding OMN-014
findings.summary: recoverInterruptedSplices now uses each record's own expected successor (address, token, amount) instead of one global observation, refuses to let two pending splices claim the same coin, rejects a successor that is not the coin already recorded for the splice, and persists the observed coin id while the successor is unconfirmed. The dead ternary is gone. Residual: the observed coin is bound by expected amount/address and the per-record coin id, not by a transaction-input proof.
findings.impact: A channel can be marked active with a coin that belongs to a different splice, or two records cleared by one coin.

repro.expected: Each pending splice recovers only its own successor.
repro.actual: Each record uses its own expected successor, a claimed-coin set prevents reuse, and a mismatched recorded coin is rejected (tests/unit/omnia-splice/src/__tests__/successor.test.ts).
evidence: packages/omnia-splice/src/successor.ts: no-op ternary in the rebroadcast result

fix.approach: Bind the successor to the splice: require the transaction id or a spent-input link, exclude coins already claimed by another recovery record, and remove the dead ternary.
constraints: Keep the CAN-012 ambiguity rejection.
A coin claimed by one splice must not be reused by another.
acceptance: Two pending splices cannot both adopt one coin.
Recovery either proves lineage or leaves the record funding_pending.

findings.title: Watchtower callbacks only emit observations; nothing protects the channel
findings.source: Omnia whole-family re-audit (2026-11-17), finding OMN-015
findings.summary: The watch handlers now act. A unilateral close is contested by broadcasting the latest signed close package (funding-coin proof plus script proof) with startUnilateralClose, recording the contest window. An expiring HTLC is timed out with timeoutHTLC, persisted, and the signed timeout state is sent to the counterparty. Both paths emit an observation with the outcome and leave the finding unprocessed if the action fails. Residual: the host-level simulation of both actions is still the acceptance test to add.
findings.impact: A unilateral close or an expiring HTLC is noticed but not acted on. The window to contest or claim can pass while the host is healthy.

repro.expected: A unilateral-close finding triggers the contest path (or an explicit, recorded refusal).
repro.actual: A close broadcasts a contest transaction (or fails closed) and an expiring HTLC is timed out and propagated; observed decisions are recorded as observation events.
evidence: packages/omnia-host/src/lifecycle.ts: both callbacks contain a single `observation.emit`
packages/omnia-host/src/watch.ts: comment claims the host wires contest logic

fix.approach: Implement (or explicitly refuse and surface) the protective action: contest with the latest signed state, timeout or fulfil an expiring HTLC, and record the decision. Make the successor check bind to the channel state rather than address+amount alone.
constraints: Do not claim watchtower support while only emitting events.
A protective action must be idempotent across restarts.
acceptance: A simulated unilateral close causes a contest broadcast (or a recorded, operator-visible refusal).
An expiring HTLC causes timeout/fulfil before the deadline.

findings.source: Omnia host signing audit, 2026-11-18 (verified against 997b7f40)
findings.title: Payments report success before the counterparty co-signs
findings.summary: omnia/pay calls updateState (a locally signed partial state), stores it, emits committed, sends STATE_UPDATE and returns success. It never waits for the peer ACK or calls attachCounterpartySignature, even though the integration ACK already carries counterpartyPartialState and the close package.
findings.impact: The API can report a payment that only one party signed. Stored balances/sequence can diverge from the last jointly enforceable state, and a rejection/timeout is invisible to the caller.

repro.expected: success is returned only after the peer co-signature is verified and durably stored.
repro.actual: methods.ts pay returns success immediately after sending the state update.

fix.approach: Add prepared → locally-signed → peer-signed → fully-validated → committed stages. Collect the ACK, merge with attachCounterpartySignature, verify the complete state/close package, persist, then report success.
constraints: Never advertise a payment on a one-party state.
Do not advance the authoritative balance until both signatures are stored.
Keep failure/timeout explicit.
acceptance: A payment succeeds only after the ACK signature is merged and verified.
A timeout/rejection returns a non-success result and leaves the prior state authoritative.
Retries are idempotent.

findings.source: Omnia host signing audit, 2026-11-18 (verified against 997b7f40)
findings.title: Exit entitlements still do not prove the witness or the authoritative pool coin
findings.summary: verifyVtxoExitEntitlement now checks the proof root/epoch, decodes the exit transaction, checks the payout address/amount and the funding input. It still does not decode/verify witness signatures or proofs, makes the digest optional (skipping transaction checks when absent), and never anchors the funding coin/exit delay to live or proven historical pool state.
findings.impact: A caller can still supply internally consistent metadata plus an unverified witness and have the helper accept an exit that does not actually provide the promised payout, unless a separate verifier checks the chain proof.

repro.expected: The exit transaction and witness are rebuilt/verified against trusted pool and owner state, with a mandatory digest.
repro.actual: Transaction shape is checked only when digest is present; witnessHex only has to be non-empty.

fix.approach: Require a digest, rebuild the canonical exit transaction from trusted pool/owner state, compare every committed field, decode and verify the witness, and anchor the funding coin and exit delay to the pool (live or historical).
constraints: Do not accept a missing digest as a bypass.
Do not trust the entitlement to describe its own pool state.
Keep historical-epoch proofs verifiable.
acceptance: A missing/different digest is rejected.
The witness is verified and the funding coin/exit delay are anchored.
A valid pool exit still passes.

findings.source: Omnia host signing audit, 2026-11-18 (verified against 997b7f40)
findings.title: An incoming message can overwrite the cached peer for an unrelated channel
findings.summary: The host cached channelPeers from any inbound message channelId before binding the peer to the channel counterparty. The cache is now updated only when the authenticated peer key is a registered party of the stored channel and is not the local identity.
findings.impact: A connected peer that names a channel id can no longer replace the routing cache and receive signed HTLC updates for that channel.

repro.expected: Only a channel counterparty can be cached for the channel.
repro.actual: Fixed: isChannelPeer checks the peer key against channel.parties and excludes the local key.

fix.approach: Derive the association from authenticated participant identity and verify it against the channel record before caching.
constraints: Never update the cache merely because a message names a channel.
Exclude the local identity.
acceptance: A foreign peer naming a channel cannot become its cached peer.
The real counterparty is still cached.

findings.source: Omnia host signing audit, 2026-11-18 (verified against 997b7f40)
findings.title: The advertised N-party factory API coordinates with only one remote participant
findings.summary: The host coordinates a factory opening with exactly one remote peer, so it now refuses anything but two distinct participants with an explicit error instead of advertising N-party coordination it cannot perform. Library builders (buildFactoryOpening) remain N-capable; only the host API is scoped.
findings.impact: A caller can no longer create a factory that only one remote learned about, or that reuses one party's signer for another. N-party factories are not available through the host until multi-peer coordination lands.

repro.expected: Every factory participant is coordinated by identity and every signature is verified.
repro.actual: assertTwoPartyFactory rejects N>2 and duplicate participants on both factory paths (tests/unit/omnia-host/src/__tests__/peer-guards.test.ts).

fix.approach: Iterate all remote participants, connect by identity, collect and verify each signature, and persist N-party progress so restarts can resume.
constraints: Do not reuse one participant’s signer for another.
Fail closed when any participant is missing.
acceptance: A 3-party factory gathers all three signatures.
Progress survives a restart.

findings.source: Deeper Omnia host audit, 2026-11-18 (verified against 41106016 / 997b7f4)
findings.title: Liquidity deposits can be credited against a coin that does not belong to the claimed LP
findings.summary: The host deposit verifier checked existence, spent state, token and amount only. It now delegates to chainProvider.verifyDeposit when available (owner address, token, amount, confirmation) and otherwise checks owner address and a positive MMR entry before accepting the commitment.
findings.impact: A claimant could previously present an unrelated observable coin and receive a position/receipt without proving ownership.

repro.expected: A coin whose address is not the claimed LP address is rejected.
repro.actual: Fixed: the deposit verifier compares the coin owner and requires chain confirmation.

fix.approach: Use the real chain-provider deposit contract (owner/token/amount/confirmation) and fail closed; do not substitute a narrower check through a cast.
constraints: Never accept a coin without matching ownership and confirmation evidence.
acceptance: Wrong-owner coin is rejected before a position is created.
The honest LP coin still deposits.

findings.source: Deeper Omnia host audit, 2026-11-18 (verified against 41106016 / 997b7f4)
findings.title: The release gate can ignore an unresolved critical finding through an alias
findings.summary: The SDK gate skipped any finding with a canonical id, without checking whether the canonical row was still blocking at the same or higher severity. OMN-001 (critical, open) was hidden behind CAN-019 (high, fixed). The gate now suppresses an alias only when its canonical row is blocking at the same or higher severity; a regression test is still pending.
findings.impact: A critical unresolved finding could be excluded from the release-blocking calculation.

repro.expected: An open alias blocks at its own severity unless a blocking canonical row covers it.
repro.actual: Fixed in verify-findings-gate.mjs and the canary gate; OMN-001 now appears in the blocking set. Regression test pending.

fix.approach: An alias inherits blocking status from the most restrictive unresolved row in its equivalence group; a fixed canonical row never suppresses an open alias.
constraints: Do not weaken the gate to make a release pass.
acceptance: OMN-001 blocks while open.
A genuinely duplicated alias is counted once.

findings.source: Deeper Omnia host audit, 2026-11-18 (verified against 41106016 / 997b7f4)
findings.title: Pool accounting can diverge between liquidity positions
findings.summary: The host stores a registry in the pool record and a copy in every position. Deposits update both, but allocation, release, withdrawal, approval and payout update only the position copy. Later deposits start from the older pool registry and can hold incompatible accounting versions at once.
findings.impact: Divergent registry versions can misstate capital and may enable double payouts depending on the settlement backend.

repro.expected: A single authoritative, versioned pool registry drives every position mutation.
repro.actual: Mutations update position.registry only; pool.registry is stale after the first non-deposit mutation.

fix.approach: Maintain one authoritative registry per pool, apply mutations through atomic versioned updates, and derive position views from it instead of copying.
constraints: Do not silently fork a pool registry per position.
acceptance: A second deposit sees the latest allocation/withdraw state.
Concurrent mutations fail on version conflict rather than overwrite.

findings.source: Deeper Omnia host audit, 2026-11-18 (verified against 41106016 / 997b7f4)
findings.title: One unspent funding coin can support multiple LP commitments
findings.summary: depositToPool verifies that the referenced coin is currently unspent but does not reserve or consume it, and the registry indexes commitments by commitment id rather than unique funding coin. The same UTXO can satisfy multiple deposits.
findings.impact: The same economic collateral can be counted multiple times, inflating pool capital and LP entitlements.

repro.expected: A funding coin can back at most one active commitment.
repro.actual: A second deposit with the same underlyingUtxoRef creates a second position/receipt.

fix.approach: Add a durable unique funding-coin reservation/consumption index scoped by chain and asset; reject duplicate active commitments and reconcile if the coin is spent/reorged.
constraints: Do not rely on a transient unspent lookup as uniqueness.
acceptance: A duplicate funding coin is rejected across pools/positions.
A spent/reorged coin invalidates the reservation.

findings.source: Deeper Omnia host audit, 2026-11-18 (verified against 41106016 / 997b7f4)
findings.title: VTXO epochs are marked published after broadcast, not chain confirmation
findings.summary: anchorBatch calls authority.markPublished(epoch) as soon as submission reports success. MinimaRpcProvider.submitTransaction reports mining/submission, not accepted-chain inclusion at depth, so the journal can record an epoch as published without confirmation and without reorg handling.
findings.impact: Downstream consumers may treat a locally recorded root as chain-backed settlement evidence when the anchor was never confirmed.

repro.expected: signed/submitted/included/confirmed/published are distinct and confirmation is checked on-chain.
repro.actual: published is set immediately after submitTransaction succeeds.

fix.approach: Separate the publication states; confirm on-chain at the required depth before markPublished; reconcile/invalidate on reorg.
constraints: Do not equate submission with confirmation.
acceptance: An unconfirmed/rejected/reorged anchor is not published.
A confirmed anchor advances only after depth is verified.

findings.source: Deeper Omnia host audit, 2026-11-18 (verified against 51aed956)
findings.title: Automatic channel funding selection compares atoms with decimal MINIMA
findings.summary: selectFundingCoin passed req.targetAmount.toString() (an atom count) to CoinSelectionService, which parses decimal MINIMA, so a 0.2 MINIMA target became roughly 2e43 MINIMA. The caller then used only selectedCoins[0]. The host now converts the target with atomsToAmount and picks a single coin that covers it; multi-input funding is reported explicitly instead of silently truncated.
findings.impact: Automatic channel funding could fail with a false insufficient-funds result, and multi-coin selection was silently dropped.

repro.expected: A 0.2 MINIMA target selects a coin covering 0.2 MINIMA.
repro.actual: Fixed: the target crosses the boundary as decimal text and one sufficient coin is chosen; multi-input selection raises an explicit error.

fix.approach: Convert the atom target back to decimal MINIMA at the selection boundary and require one coin that covers the target, with an explicit multi-input error.
constraints: Do not drop selected inputs silently.
Never pass an atom integer to a decimal-MINIMA API.
acceptance: A fractional target selects a sufficient single coin.
Multi-input selection fails explicitly.

findings.source: Deeper Omnia host audit, 2026-11-18 (verified against 51aed956)
findings.title: Factory RPCs interpret contributions as atoms instead of decimal amounts
findings.summary: prepareFactory and createFactory used BigInt(requiredString(item, "contributionAmount")), unlike every other host monetary parameter. A decimal fraction was rejected and a whole number meant that many atoms. Both handlers now use rpcAmountToAtoms.
findings.impact: Fractional contributions were rejected and whole numbers were treated as atoms, corrupting totalValue, allocations and escape shares.

repro.expected: A 0.2 MINIMA contribution is accepted as 0.2 MINIMA.
repro.actual: Fixed: both factory paths convert at the RPC boundary.

fix.approach: Convert every participant contribution with rpcAmountToAtoms and cover both the prepared and one-shot factory paths.
constraints: Do not mix atom and decimal contribution paths.
acceptance: Fractional contributions produce atom allocations.
Oversized atom integers are rejected.

findings.source: Deeper Omnia host audit, 2026-11-18 (verified against 51aed956)
findings.title: Inbound HTLC validation compared the proposed state with itself
findings.summary: _handleStateUpdate replaced the persisted pendingHTLCs with the peer-supplied set before verifyStateForCoSign, so validateHtlcSet compared proposed HTLC terms with themselves. Verification now uses the persisted channel; the proposed set is only used for digest/signature construction.
findings.impact: A counterparty could retain an HTLC id while changing its hashlock, timeout, amount or parties and still be co-signed.

repro.expected: Verification receives the persisted HTLC set.
repro.actual: Fixed: verifyState/verifyStateForCoSign receives the original channel.

fix.approach: Validate against the persisted channel and keep the proposed state only for digest construction.
constraints: New HTLC ids remain valid; existing ids may only transition forward.
acceptance: A mutated existing HTLC term is rejected.
A new HTLC is still accepted.

findings.source: Deeper Omnia host audit, 2026-11-18 (verified against 51aed956)
findings.title: Crash recovery could lose the signing watermark after a WOTS signature was released
findings.summary: The double-sign guard was an in-memory watermark plus a pendingProposal field persisted after signing. A crash after signState but before the channel was stored could forget the signed state and allow a different payload at the same sequence. An append-only signing intent is now recorded before the signer is invoked, the signed state is persisted before the ACK, and an unresolved attempt blocks conflicting payloads after restart.
findings.impact: Two conflicting states for one sequence could be signed after a restart.

repro.expected: A durable signing-intent record exists before the signer is invoked and blocks conflicting payloads after restart.
repro.actual: Fixed: beginSigningAttempt runs before prepare/sign; integration persists before ACK.

fix.approach: Persist an append-only signing intent before signing, persist the signed state before the ACK, and block conflicting attempts after restart. Hosts supply a durable journal.
constraints: Never sign two payloads for one sequence.
An attempt with a released signature can never be abandoned.
acceptance: Crash injection after signing cannot produce a conflicting signature.
An identical payload replay is still allowed.

findings.source: Deeper Omnia host audit, 2026-11-18 (verified against 51aed956)
findings.title: The host could issue active VTXOs without verified on-chain backing
findings.summary: createVtxoPool accepted a caller-declared totalCapacity without funding proof, and mintVtxo persisted an active VTXO without verifying pool backing or operator authorization. Pool creation now requires a confirmed, unspent coin covering the capacity; mints are conserved against that backing and stay provisional until the operator co-signs the receipt.
findings.impact: The local ledger could represent transferable liabilities with no on-chain pool coin behind them.

repro.expected: A VTXO becomes active only after confirmed pool backing and the operator receipt.
repro.actual: Fixed: backing is chain-verified, mints are conserved, provisional until the receipt is signed.

fix.approach: Separate provisional issuance from transferable claims; require confirmed backing, conservation and the operator receipt before active.
constraints: Never advertise unbacked VTXOs as redeemable.
Re-verify the backing coin is unspent at mint time.
acceptance: An unfunded pool is rejected.
Capacity above the backing coin is rejected.
Mints stay provisional until co-signed.

findings.source: Deeper Omnia host audit, 2026-11-18 (verified against 51aed956)
findings.title: VTXO exits could be marked complete without proving a payout
findings.summary: completeVtxoExit called markExited with an optional caller txpowId; neither the host nor markExited checked the exit transaction, funding coin, payout or confirmations. Completion now requires a mandatory transaction id and a trusted verifier that confirms owner, amount, token and depth; the VTXO stays exiting otherwise.
findings.impact: The VTXO ledger could report settlement finality with no corresponding payment.

repro.expected: Exit completion requires verified chain evidence.
repro.actual: Fixed: completeVtxoExit requires a verifier and markExited requires a transaction id.

fix.approach: Require a trusted verifier for the exact exit transaction, funding input, owner output, amount/token and depth; keep exiting until verified.
constraints: No caller assertion may finalize an exit.
acceptance: An unverified exit stays exiting.
A verified exit becomes exited.
A wrong owner or shallow confirmation is rejected.

findings.source: Deeper Omnia covenant/transaction audit, 2026-11-18 (verified against 51aed956)
findings.title: Recreating a VTXO pool with the same identity reset its capacity and commitment history
findings.summary: createVtxoPool unconditionally stored a freshly initialized pool under its deterministic id, so repeating the request reset available capacity, epoch and the membership set while earlier VTXOs stayed in the store. Creation is now create-only: an identical repeat returns the existing pool, and different terms are rejected.
findings.impact: Capacity could be re-issued while orphaning the original membership history.

repro.expected: A repeated pool creation never resets capacity, epoch or members.
repro.actual: Fixed: the existing pool is returned (existed:true); conflicting terms are rejected.

fix.approach: Make creation create-only and idempotent for identical terms.
constraints: Never reset capacity, epoch or members through the creation endpoint.
acceptance: A repeat returns the existing pool.
Different terms are rejected.
Capacity and members are unchanged.

findings.source: Deeper Omnia covenant/transaction audit, 2026-11-18 (verified against 51aed956)
findings.title: VTXO refresh could overwrite its own input because the id excluded the epoch
findings.summary: computeVtxoId ignored the epoch, so reusing the mint nonce made the refreshed output id equal to the input id and the host stored the replacement over the consumed record. Replacement ids now include the epoch, and a refresh that would reproduce its input id is rejected.
findings.impact: A consumed VTXO id could become active again, making proof and status history ambiguous.

repro.expected: A refresh always produces a distinct id.
repro.actual: Fixed: epoch is part of replacement ids; same-id refreshes throw.

fix.approach: Include the epoch in replacement ids and reject an output id equal to the input.
constraints: Mint ids stay stable; only replacements carry an epoch.
acceptance: Refreshing with the mint nonce yields a new id.
The consumed record is preserved.

findings.source: Deeper Omnia covenant/transaction audit, 2026-11-18 (verified against 51aed956)
findings.title: Operator receipt signing broke after the first mint into a VTXO pool
findings.summary: Mint roots commit every accumulated pool member, but the receipt payload was verified against a root rebuilt from only the receipt outputs, so the second mint could not be co-signed. Receipts now verify outputs against the pool member set and the pool root.
findings.impact: Issuance and operator authorization diverged after the first mint.

repro.expected: The second mint in a pool prepares a valid receipt.
repro.actual: Fixed: batch verification accepts the authoritative member set.

fix.approach: Verify receipt outputs against the pool member leaves and the pool root; the host passes its authoritative set.
constraints: A receipt must never be verified against a root it supplied itself.
acceptance: Second and later mints co-sign.
An output outside the member set is rejected.

findings.source: Deeper Omnia covenant/transaction audit, 2026-11-18 (verified against 51aed956)
findings.title: Duplicate incoming state updates could consume multiple WOTS key pairs at the same sequence
findings.summary: STATE_UPDATE handling was not serialized per channel, so identical retries each reserved and committed two WOTS leaves. Inbound updates are now serialized per channel and identical (channel, sequence, commitment) retries reuse the recorded ACK instead of signing again.
findings.impact: Signing capacity could be consumed without advancing the channel, and one logical update could yield several ACK signatures.

repro.expected: An identical retry reuses the recorded reply.
repro.actual: Fixed: per-channel serialization plus a reply cache.

fix.approach: Serialize per channel and key replies by sequence+commitment.
constraints: Never reserve a second pair of leaves for one commitment.
acceptance: Identical retries produce one signature.
Both retries receive an ACK.

findings.source: Deeper Omnia covenant/transaction audit, 2026-11-18 (verified against 51aed956)
findings.title: Prepared-signature submissions did not prevent one-time WOTS key reuse
findings.summary: submitPay accepted wallet-supplied update and settlement indices without checking they differ or were previously consumed. It now rejects identical leaves and, when a durable leaf registry is configured, rejects a leaf reused for a different digest.
findings.impact: One WOTS leaf could sign two different transaction digests.

repro.expected: Update and settlement signatures use disjoint, unconsumed leaves.
repro.actual: Fixed: indices must differ and consumed leaves are tracked per digest.

fix.approach: Require disjoint indices and record consumed leaves against their digest.
constraints: A leaf may only ever sign one digest.
acceptance: Equal indices are rejected.
A leaf reused for another digest is rejected.

findings.source: Deeper Omnia covenant/transaction audit, 2026-11-18 (verified against 51aed956)
findings.title: Recreating a liquidity pool could erase its authoritative registry
findings.summary: createLiquidityPool built a fresh empty registry and overwrote any existing pool with the same id. Creation is now create-only: an identical repeat returns the existing manifest and registry, and a different capacity is rejected.
findings.impact: Deposits, allocations, withdrawals and receipts could be erased while positions survived.

repro.expected: A repeated creation preserves the existing registry.
repro.actual: Fixed: existing pools are returned unchanged.

fix.approach: Create-only pool ids with a fresh-registry check.
constraints: Never overwrite a registry through the creation endpoint.
acceptance: Registry survives a repeat.
A conflicting capacity is rejected.

findings.source: Deeper Omnia covenant/transaction audit, 2026-11-18 (verified against 51aed956)
findings.title: Splice-in proposals omitted the additional coin address
findings.summary: proposeSpliceIn accepted a coin id and amount but no address, and the builder wrote an empty address placeholder. The address is now a required parameter, carried into the proposal, and the host resolves and verifies the coin (owner, amount, unspent) before proposing.
findings.impact: The standard splice-in path produced transaction bytes that did not describe the added coin.

repro.expected: A splice-in carrying no address is rejected; a real address is encoded.
repro.actual: Fixed: the builder fails closed and the host verifies the coin.

fix.approach: Require the address, carry it through the proposal, and verify the coin on chain.
constraints: Never serialize a placeholder address.
acceptance: Missing address throws.
The encoded input carries the real address.

findings.source: Deeper Omnia covenant/transaction audit, 2026-11-18 (verified against 51aed956)
findings.title: Liquidity deposits could be marked chain-confirmed without requiring confirmation
findings.summary: The deposit verifier never set requireConfirmed, and evaluateDeposit only gated on confirmation when asked. The host now requires confirmation and a real depth (created vs tip), rejects verifier results that report confirmed:false, and the fallback path fails when depth cannot be established.
findings.impact: An unconfirmed or reorg-prone coin could back an active liquidity position.

repro.expected: Only a coin confirmed at depth backs a position.
repro.actual: Fixed: confirmation and depth are mandatory at every funding check.

fix.approach: Add minConfirmations/chainTip to the deposit contract and require them for liquidity funding.
constraints: Never treat a positive MMR entry as depth.
acceptance: A mempool coin is rejected.
Unknown depth is rejected.
A deep coin is accepted.

findings.source: Deeper Omnia covenant/transaction audit, 2026-11-18 (verified against 51aed956)
findings.title: VTXO transfers and refreshes produced active claims absent from the pool commitment
findings.summary: Minting appended to the pool member set, but transfer and refresh outputs kept single-batch proofs and were stored active without joining it. A pool transition primitive now consumes inputs and adds outputs at a new epoch, and the host applies it before persisting.
findings.impact: Active VTXOs could fail membership verification and existing claims were not anchored.

repro.expected: Transfer/refresh outputs are committed by the pool.
repro.actual: Fixed: transitionPoolMembers consumes inputs, adds outputs and republishes the root.

fix.approach: Add an atomic membership transition and use it for transfer and refresh.
constraints: A consumed id can never re-enter the set.
Each transition publishes a new epoch root.
acceptance: Outputs verify against the pool.
Consumed inputs leave the set.
Receipts prepare after the transition.

findings.source: Deeper Omnia covenant/transaction audit, 2026-11-18 (verified against 51aed956)
findings.title: A unilateral VTXO exit could alter the remaining pool root and epoch
findings.summary: The individual-exit branch returned before asserting the successor commitment root or epoch, so an exit could leave a residual pool whose membership matched no published state. Both ports are now preserved in every holder exit branch.
findings.impact: Holders could lose proof continuity after another holder exited.

repro.expected: An individual exit preserves STATE(100) and STATE(101).
repro.actual: Fixed: the exit branch asserts both are unchanged.

fix.approach: Assert root and epoch preservation inside the exit branch, before any RETURN.
constraints: The cooperative branch keeps its monotone epoch rule.
acceptance: Every holder exit branch carries both assertions.

findings.source: Deeper Omnia covenant/transaction audit, 2026-11-18 (verified against 51aed956)
findings.title: VTXO on-chain spending helpers broadcast without required proofs
findings.summary: Anchor, per-share exit and owner-pool transactions treated coin/script proofs as optional and broadcast an empty witness. All three now refuse to broadcast unless proofs are supplied.
findings.impact: Malformed recovery transactions could be produced and submitted.

repro.expected: Broadcasting without proofs is rejected.
repro.actual: Fixed: assertBroadcastProofs gates every broadcast path.

fix.approach: Require proofs for every spending input before broadcasting.
constraints: Offline draft generation may still omit them.
acceptance: Each helper throws without proofs.

findings.source: Deeper Omnia covenant/transaction audit, 2026-11-18 (verified against 51aed956)
findings.title: Funding activation did not consistently wait for chain confirmations
findings.summary: The receiver checked confirmation depth, but the initiator marked a channel active on mere observation and the factory finalizer committed immediately after submission. Both now require depth; a channel or factory whose funding is not confirmed stays opening.
findings.impact: Operational channels or factories could rest on unconfirmed funding.

repro.expected: Activation requires the funding coin at depth.
repro.actual: Fixed: both paths gate on confirmations (default 1).

fix.approach: Apply one finality rule: submitted → observed → confirmed → active.
constraints: Submission is not confirmation.
acceptance: Shallow funding stays opening.
Deep funding activates.

findings.source: OMN-058 feasibility spike, 2026-11-18 (RFC-079)
findings.title: KISSVM CHECKSIG ignores its documented data and signature arguments
findings.summary: Minima documents and implements CHECKSIG(public_key data signature): exactly three HEX parameters, verified as TreeKey.verify(data, signature). The SDK evaluator ignored args[1]/args[2] and verified the witness signature over the transaction digest. TypeScript now enforces the reference semantics (tree signature, or a flat WOTS signature over the supplied data) and Rust/WASM does the same for the flat form; both reject 0/1-argument forms, zero-length operands and non-hex operands.
findings.impact: Detached certificates could not be authenticated, so a contestable factory escape (OMN-058) was unimplementable. Scripts that passed locally under the witness-only form would have failed on a real node.

repro.expected: CHECKSIG(pk data sig) verifies the supplied signature over the supplied data.
repro.actual: Fixed: the evaluator verifies the supplied data and signature. The parity suite measures TS against the Rust/WASM artifact on the same fixtures; the node leg is scripts/kissvm-node-parity.mjs.

fix.approach: Implement the reference three-argument form while keeping SIGNEDBY as the witness path, and prove TS/Rust agreement with shared fixtures generated from real keys.
constraints: Do not silently keep the current meaning under the documented signature.
Cover both the witness path and the detached path with real signatures.
acceptance: CHECKSIG(pk data sig) returns true only for a valid signature over data.
A stale or foreign certificate fails.
The witness cannot change the verdict.
0/1-argument and zero-length forms are rejected.
TypeScript and Rust/WASM agree on every supported fixture.

findings.source: Omnia SDK audit — 25 November 2026, reporter finding OMN-066
findings.title: LSP quotes are issued against advertised capacity with no durable reservation
findings.summary: The admission policy documents that it does not reserve capacity and that the provider must re-check before co-signing. The facade implements neither the reservation nor the re-check: every quote() call is evaluated against the same static manifest, so N concurrent quotes can each be within capacity while their sum is not.
findings.impact: Concurrent requests can collectively exceed available liquidity. Host-level coin selection bounds what can be funded on chain, but it does not enforce a commercial exposure limit and fails late, after a consumer has been given a signed commitment.

repro.expected: Issuing a quote reserves its provider-side amount against a durable ledger, and the reservation is released on expiry, consumed on open and reconciled after restart.
repro.actual: Two quote() calls for the same asset at maxChannel both succeed; nothing records the first commitment.
evidence: packages/omnia-lsp-provider/src/policy.ts:62-67 — the policy states it does not reserve capacity

fix.approach: Add a reservation ledger keyed by quoteId with amount, expiry and state (reserved/consumed/released). Reserve on issue, release on expiry, consume atomically on open, and reconcile entries that outlive a restart. Capacity checks subtract outstanding reservations.
constraints: Reservation state must be durable, not in-process memory.
Expiry must use the provider clock, not the request's.
A failed open must release, not leak, its reservation.
acceptance: Concurrent quotes cannot exceed the provider's per-asset exposure limit.
An expired reservation stops counting against capacity.
A restart re-reads outstanding reservations instead of resetting exposure.
The open path re-checks capacity against the live ledger.

findings.source: Omnia SDK audit — 25 November 2026, reporter finding OMN-067
findings.title: Manifest freshness is decided with a caller-supplied clock
findings.summary: evaluateOpenRequest() reads `request.now` and falls back to Date.now(). The expiry check that protects the provider is therefore under the requester's control: an expired manifest can be made to look current by setting now to a past timestamp.
findings.impact: The provider can be made to serve terms it has withdrawn. The same field is also carried through the open request type, so the attack needs no special access.

repro.expected: Freshness is decided by the provider's trusted clock; a time source is injectable for tests through configuration only.
repro.actual: evaluateOpenRequest(manifest, { ...request, now: 1 }) treats a manifest whose expiresAt is in the past as valid.

fix.approach: Remove `now` from the public request type. Thread the provider clock (already available as config.now in createOmniaLspProvider) into evaluateOpenRequest as an explicit parameter.
constraints: Keep deterministic tests possible via the config clock.
Do not silently ignore a caller-supplied now: reject the field if it is still accepted structurally.
acceptance: A request cannot influence the manifest expiry check.
The facade's clock injection still works for tests.
The public request type no longer exposes a time source.

findings.source: Omnia SDK audit — 25 November 2026, reporter finding OMN-068
findings.title: Host adapter reports success for an undefined, malformed or error-only response
findings.summary: createOmniaHostProviderHost() defines success as `result?.success !== false`. An undefined return, a response object with no success field, or an object carrying only an error is therefore classified as a successful open or close.
findings.impact: A failed or unrecognised host response is reported to the consumer as success, so the LSP layer believes a channel exists (or was closed) when it does not. Callers that key funding or accounting off this flag act on a false positive.

repro.expected: Success requires an explicit success flag plus operation-specific evidence: a channelId for open, a terminal lifecycle state for close.
repro.actual: A handler returning undefined, {}, or { error: 'boom' } is reported as { success: true }.

fix.approach: Require result.success === true and, for open, a non-empty channelId; for close, a status that proves the channel reached a closing/closed state. Treat a non-object response as HOST_PROTOCOL_ERROR.
constraints: Fail closed on an unrecognised response shape.
Do not invent a channelId when the host omitted one.
Preserve errorCode passthrough so callers can distinguish causes.
acceptance: undefined, null, non-object and error-only responses are failures.
open success without a channelId is a failure.
A malformed host result cannot reach the consumer as success.

findings.source: Omnia SDK audit — 25 November 2026, reporter finding OMN-069
findings.title: Quote validation establishes shape, not authenticity
findings.summary: validateOpenQuote() requires only that signature is a non-empty string and that termsHash is 32 bytes. Neither is recomputed or verified. quoteMatchesManifest() compares provider identity, settlement address and token offering, and states in its own doc comment that it is not a substitute for manifest verification. The package exposes no API that verifies a quote's signature or its terms commitment.
findings.impact: Every consumer of the LSP layer inherits an authenticity gap: a structurally valid quote cannot be distinguished from a forged one. This is the missing primitive that OMN-066 needs to close its authorization boundary.

repro.expected: A canonical verifyOpenQuote(quote, manifest, { now }) recomputes termsHash from the quoted fields, verifies the provider signature over it with the manifest identity key, and checks freshness.
repro.actual: A quote with signature 'not-a-signature' and an arbitrary termsHash passes validateOpenQuote() and quoteMatchesManifest().
evidence: packages/omnia-lsp/src/quote.ts:114 — signature must be a non-empty string
packages/omnia-lsp/src/quote.ts:152-170 — quoteMatchesManifest compares identity fields only
no verifyOpenQuote export exists in packages/omnia-lsp/src/index.ts

fix.approach: Add verifyOpenQuote(quote, manifest, options) that rebuilds the canonical terms object, recomputes the hash with the same domain separator used at issue time, verifies the signature through an injected verifier, and returns structured errors. Keep structural validation separate and name it as such.
constraints: The canonical terms serialisation must be byte-identical to createUnsignedOpenQuote.
Signature verification stays runtime-neutral via injection, matching signOpenQuote.
Do not make validateOpenQuote imply authenticity in its name or docs.
acceptance: A mutated amount, fee, token, expiry or consumer identity is detected by the recomputed terms hash.
A signature from a key other than the manifest identity key is rejected.
A verifier that throws produces a structured failure, not an exception.
Round-tripping a provider-issued quote verifies.

findings.source: Omnia SDK audit — 25 November 2026, reporter finding OMN-070
findings.title: LSP fee admission and fee calculation ignore the flat fee and the provider's contribution
findings.summary: Admission compares only manifest.fees.openBps with request.maxOpenFeeBps, so a flat opening fee is never checked against the consumer's ceiling. Quote construction then computes openFee and leaseFee from request.localAmount (the consumer side) even though the provider is the party supplying the liquidity the lease is priced on.
findings.impact: A consumer can be charged more than its stated maximum when the manifest carries a flat fee, and the provider's fee revenue is sized off the counterparty's deposit rather than its own commitment. Both directions of the commercial terms are wrong.

repro.expected: The maximum-fee check covers the total the consumer will pay, expressed in token atoms, and the fee basis is explicit in the signed terms.
repro.actual: With openFlat set and maxOpenFeeBps 0, admission passes and the quote charges the flat fee. Changing remoteAmount does not change the lease fee.
evidence: packages/omnia-lsp-provider/src/quote.ts:52-58 — openFee from openFlat/openBps, leaseFee from localAmount

fix.approach: Compute the full fee schedule for the request, compare its atom total against a maximum expressed in atoms, and state the fee basis (consumer contribution vs total channel value vs provider commitment) explicitly in the signed terms so the consumer can verify what it agreed to.
constraints: Do not mix basis points and flat amounts in one unchecked comparison.
Fees must be derivable from the signed terms alone.
Changing a fee basis is a wire change: version the terms object.
acceptance: A flat opening fee above the consumer's ceiling is refused at admission.
The quote's fee fields match the schedule admission approved.
The fee basis is explicit and covered by the terms hash.

findings.source: Omnia SDK audit — 25 November 2026, reporter finding OMN-073
findings.title: The pending splice journal does not record its expected successor
findings.summary: PendingSpliceRecord has an `expected` field carrying the successor address, token and amount, and recoverInterruptedSplices() prefers it. finalizeSplice() writes its recovery record without populating it, so recovery falls back to the globally supplied observation parameters.
findings.impact: When more than one splice is interrupted, recovery can reconcile one splice against another splice's expected successor — accepting a coin with the right shape but the wrong channel. The journal that exists to make recovery specific is not used in practice.

repro.expected: Every production journal entry names the successor it expects.
repro.actual: The record written at broadcast time has no `expected` field, and recoverInterruptedSplices falls through to the caller-supplied address/token/amount.

fix.approach: Compute the expected successor descriptor from the splice terms at journal-write time and make the field mandatory in the type, so a store cannot persist a record without it.
constraints: Recovery must never use a global observation for a record that has its own expectation.
Store atomically with the tx hex and txpow id already written.
acceptance: The journal record written before broadcast contains the expected successor.
Two interrupted splices recover against their own expectations.
A legacy record without `expected` is rejected or migrated explicitly, not silently defaulted.

findings.source: Omnia SDK audit — 25 November 2026, reporter finding OMN-074
findings.title: The splice journal is cleared before the successor channel is persisted
findings.summary: finalizeSplice() clears the pending record as soon as the successor is observed as active, and only then builds and returns the SplicedChannel object that the caller persists. A crash in that window leaves the predecessor channel in local state, the successor on chain and no recovery record.
findings.impact: The failure is unrecoverable without manual chain inspection: the host resumes with a channel whose funding coin is spent, and nothing tells it a splice completed. It is exactly the state the journal exists to prevent.

repro.command: cd artifacts/canary && pnpm run canary run 34-omnia-host-durability
repro.expected: Journal completion, predecessor retirement and successor persistence commit together; a crash before commit leaves the splice pending and recoverable.
repro.actual: pendingSpliceStore.clear() runs before splicedChannel is constructed and before the caller can store it.

fix.approach: Reorder so the successor is constructed and durably persisted, the predecessor is marked spliced, and the journal entry is cleared last. Where the host owns the store, pass a completion callback so the journal is cleared only after the channel store commits.
constraints: Never clear the journal before the successor is durable.
Keep the operation idempotent: a re-run with the journal still present must converge.
Do not leave the predecessor active after a successful commit.
acceptance: A crash injected between observation and persistence leaves a recoverable journal entry.
A successful finalize persists the successor before clearing the journal.
Recovery from either crash window converges on the same splicing state.
verificationPostPublish: cd artifacts/canary && pnpm run canary run 34-omnia-host-durability

findings.source: Omnia SDK audit — 25 November 2026, reporter finding OMN-075
findings.title: Operation replay verification loses its receiver and throws instead of returning the committed result
findings.summary: withOperation() reads verifyRequest off the operation store into a local variable and calls it as a bare function. OperationStore.verifyRequest() calls this.get(), so the call throws TypeError. Any RPC retried with an existing operationId therefore fails instead of returning the previously committed result. The unit tests missed it because they stub the store with an object literal whose verifyRequest is a closure.
findings.impact: The host's idempotency guarantee does not hold for the real SQLite-backed store: a client that retries after a timeout gets an error rather than the committed result, and cannot tell whether the operation ran. Only the operationId path is affected.

repro.expected: A retried operation with an identical request returns the stored result.
repro.actual: On the real OperationStore the retry throws TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'get').
evidence: packages/omnia-host/src/lifecycle.ts:236 — production constructs a real OperationStore
tests/unit/omnia-host/src/__tests__/mutations.test.ts:233 — mock uses a closure, so it cannot catch this

fix.approach: Call the method on the store (or bind it). Add a regression test that replays an operation through a real OperationStore on a temp sqlite file, not a stubbed object.
constraints: Do not change OperationStore's contract to accommodate an unbound call.
Keep the conflict error for a genuinely different request.
The regression test must not mock the store.
acceptance: Replaying a committed operation through the real store returns its result.
Replaying with different params still raises OperationConflictError.
A test exercises the real store and would fail against the unbound call.
