findings.source: Omnia SDK audit — 25 November 2026, reporter finding OMN-076
findings.title: An observability failure can strand a committed operation or misreport it as failed
findings.summary: withOperation() emits operation.executing outside the protected block, so a rejecting observer leaves the operation in `executing` with nothing to drive it forward. Inside the try it records `committed` and then awaits operation.committed; if that emit rejects, the catch attempts executing→failed on a record that is already `committed`, which throws an invalid-transition error.
findings.impact: Observer failure is observers' business, but here it changes the financial lifecycle: an operation that committed can be reported as failed and become unreplayable, and an operation can stall in `executing` before any work started.

repro.expected: Observability delivery cannot change the authoritative operation state; a rejecting observer is recorded and the operation still commits or fails on its own merits.
repro.actual: With an observer that throws on operation.committed, the RPC rejects even though run() succeeded and the record is `committed`; with one that throws on operation.executing, the record stays `executing`.

fix.approach: Route all observer delivery through a non-throwing boundary (or a transactional outbox) so a failed emit is recorded and retried without affecting the state machine. Move the executing emit inside a protected block and never transition committed→failed.
constraints: Observer failure must not be able to change or roll back an authoritative transition.
Do not swallow observer errors silently: surface them on the observability channel.
Keep the committed result readable even when the emit failed.
acceptance: A throwing observer cannot make a committed operation report failure.
A throwing observer cannot leave an operation stuck in `executing` before run().
Observer failures appear as their own recorded health signal.

findings.source: Omnia SDK audit — 25 November 2026, reporter finding OMN-077
findings.title: An operation whose financial side effect is unknown is classified as a retryable failure
findings.summary: withOperation() catches every exception from run() and moves the operation to `failed`, and the retry guard accepts `pending` and `failed`. There is no distinction between a failure before a financial side effect and a failure after signing, broadcasting or a remote party accepting. The store's status union already includes `unknown`, but nothing sets it.
findings.impact: Retrying after an ambiguous failure can repeat a financial side effect. The host relies entirely on each handler being individually careful, which the register already shows is not the case (CAN-022, OMN-077).

repro.expected: A handler that cannot prove whether its side effect occurred leaves the operation in a reconciling state, and retry is refused until reconciliation says it did not happen.
repro.actual: Any exception yields status `failed`, which the retry guard accepts on the next call.
evidence: packages/omnia-host/src/stores/operations.ts:5 — `unknown` exists in OperationStatus but is never written

fix.approach: Introduce an explicit unknown-outcome state. Handlers (or the RPC layer) declare the point after which an error is ambiguous; withOperation records `unknown` and refuses retry until a reconciliation step resolves it to committed or failed.
constraints: Fail closed: ambiguity is not retried.
Reconciliation must be able to consult the chain and the peer, not only local state.
Do not let an `unknown` operation be silently re-executed by a client retry.
acceptance: A failure after broadcast/sign/remote-accept records `unknown`.
A retry against `unknown` is refused with an actionable error.
Reconciliation resolves `unknown` to committed or failed with evidence.
A failure before any side effect remains plainly retryable.

findings.source: Omnia SDK audit — 25 November 2026, reporter finding OMN-078
findings.title: Route validation checks each hop and never the path
findings.summary: validateRoute() iterates route.hops and validates each in isolation. It does not require any hops, does not check that consecutive hops connect, does not check the route starts at the payer and ends at the requested recipient for the requested amount and asset, and does not check that amounts and token transitions are consistent along the path. executeMultiHopPayment() then locks only non-swap hops, so a swap-only route validates and settles nothing.
findings.impact: An empty route returns { success: true, state: 'recipient-settled', settledHops: [] } — a payment reported as settled with no value moved. A route whose hops are individually valid but disconnected can also pass, so the payment fails partway with locks already placed.

repro.command: cd artifacts/canary && pnpm run canary run 13-omnia-router-single-hop
repro.expected: A route that does not begin at the payer, end at the recipient, transport the requested amount in a consistent asset, or contain hops at all is refused before any HTLC is locked.
repro.actual: validateRoute({ hops: [] }) returns ok, and executeMultiHopPayment returns success with settledHops [].
evidence: packages/omnia-router/src/route-validation.ts:116-127 — loop over hops, no path invariant

fix.approach: Validate the route against the payment request, not only the channel graph: non-empty, hop[i].to === hop[i+1].from, first hop starts at the payer, last hop ends at request.recipient for request.token/amount, amounts non-increasing after fees, and every token transition either identical or an explicit swap. Refuse a route with no executable hops.
constraints: Do not change the channel-graph checks; add request-level invariants.
An empty or non-executable route is a failure, never a success.
Acceptance is bound to the PaymentRequest, not to a mutable hop object.
acceptance: An empty route is rejected.
A disconnected route is rejected before the first lock.
A route that does not deliver the requested amount and token to the recipient is rejected.
A swap-only route cannot return success with no settlement.
verificationPostPublish: cd artifacts/canary && pnpm run canary run 14-omnia-router-multi-hop

findings.source: Omnia SDK audit — 25 November 2026, reporter finding OMN-079
findings.title: Consecutive HTLC deadlines differ by one block in multi-hop and cross-token execution
findings.summary: Both execution paths derive each hop's timeout as expiryBlock - i (and - pos++ in the cross-token path). The gap between adjacent hops is therefore exactly one block, independent of the channel contest period, confirmation policy or the time an intermediary needs to claim or refund.
findings.impact: An intermediary can be left unable to claim an outgoing HTLC before it must refund the incoming one, or unable to act at all under network disruption. The safety margin the protocol depends on is one block.

repro.command: cd artifacts/canary && pnpm run canary run 36-omnia-real-multi-hop
repro.expected: The expiry delta is derived from the channel contest delay plus the confirmation and recovery requirements, and is validated as sufficient before locking.
repro.actual: Hops are one block apart regardless of contestDelayBlocks (normally 256).

fix.approach: Compute the required delta from the channel's contest delay and the recovery policy, expose it as a policy input with a safe default, and refuse a route whose available expiry window cannot fit every hop.
constraints: Never reduce the existing spread.
The delta must come from channel terms the router can verify, not a caller-chosen constant.
A route that cannot fit the window is rejected, not truncated.
acceptance: Consecutive HTLC deadlines are separated by at least the contest delay plus the recovery margin.
A route with insufficient expiry window is refused before locking.
Both execution paths use the same derivation.
verificationPostPublish: cd artifacts/canary && pnpm run canary run 36-omnia-real-multi-hop

findings.source: Omnia SDK audit — 25 November 2026, reporter finding OMN-080
findings.title: Rollback silently drops a locked HTLC when its channel or lease provider is missing
findings.summary: cancelHtlcs() skips a locked HTLC entirely when the channel is absent from the map or no lease provider is registered for it. It does not add the obligation to pendingRefunds, so the caller is told that rollback completed while the lock remains.
findings.impact: Liquidity stays locked with no record. The caller receives a failure result that implies recovery, and no later pass reconciles the stranded HTLC. CAN-015 covers the early-timeout part of this path; the missing-dependency branch is still open.

repro.command: cd artifacts/canary && pnpm run canary run 23-chaos-recovery
repro.expected: Every lock that rollback could not release is reported to the caller and persisted for reconciliation.
repro.actual: With the lease provider removed from the map, cancelHtlcs returns without pushing a pendingRefund.
evidence: packages/omnia-router/src/execute.ts:67-82 — only a thrown timeoutHTLC becomes a pendingRefund

fix.approach: Treat a missing channel or lease provider as an unresolved refund obligation: record it with the reason, surface it in pendingRefunds, and make it reconcilable once the dependency is available.
constraints: Do not silently skip any locked HTLC.
Keep the existing pendingRefunds shape and reason field.
A rollback that leaves locks behind must not report a clean failure.
acceptance: A lock with a missing channel or lease provider appears in pendingRefunds.
The failed result carries the unresolved obligations.
Reconciliation can release the lock once the dependency returns.
verificationPostPublish: cd artifacts/canary && pnpm run canary run 23-chaos-recovery

findings.source: Omnia SDK audit — 25 November 2026, reporter finding OMN-081
findings.title: Router fee proofs hash descriptive fields and are not settlement evidence
findings.summary: buildRouterFeeProof() builds a canonical JSON hash over channelId, htlcId, recipient, amount, tokenId and settledAt, and nothing else. The hash proves the supplied data is internally consistent; it carries no authentication from either channel party and no reference to the state transition that actually paid the intermediary.
findings.impact: Any downstream accounting that treats proofHash as evidence of earned routing income is unsound: the record can be produced for a payment that never settled. recordPoolFee consumes this structure, so pool income accounting inherits the weakness.

repro.expected: A fee proof binds the authenticated predecessor and successor channel states, both parties' authorization and the net amount the intermediary retained.
repro.actual: The proof is a self-consistent hash of caller-supplied fields; it verifies for an HTLC that was never fulfilled.

fix.approach: Attach the signed state transition (predecessor and successor state hashes, both signatures) and the fee actually retained, and verify both when the proof is consumed. Keep the current hash as an integrity check of the envelope, not as the evidence.
constraints: Do not describe an unauthenticated hash as a settlement proof in API names or docs.
Fee accounting must refuse a proof without verified bilateral authorization.
Keep backwards compatibility explicit: version the proof.
acceptance: A proof for an unfulfilled HTLC fails verification.
A proof with one party's signature missing fails verification.
Pool fee accounting refuses an unverified proof.
The retained fee is derived from the state delta, not asserted.

findings.source: Omnia SDK audit — 25 November 2026, reporter finding OMN-082
findings.title: Forwarding admission is a check-then-write across awaits, not an atomic reservation
findings.summary: The forwarder checks the in-memory link set and the journal for a duplicate hashlock or incoming HTLC, then awaits and writes the intent in a separate operation. The journal serialises individual writes, so two concurrent forwards can both pass the duplicate check and the second write then overwrites the first entry.
findings.impact: Duplicate forwarding admission. Other channel guards may prevent a doubled signature, but the forwarding journal — the record recovery depends on — is silently replaced, so one incoming HTLC can lose its outgoing association.

repro.command: cd artifacts/canary && pnpm run canary run 38-omnia-relay-phase-a
repro.expected: A reserveForward() operation performs the uniqueness check and the intent write in one atomic step.
repro.actual: Two concurrent forwards for one hashlock both observe no duplicate and both write an intent.
evidence: packages/omnia-relay/src/forwarder.ts:219-243 — duplicate check, then awaits, then record(intent)
packages/omnia-relay/src/link-journal.ts:75-87 — write is serialised but not check-and-reserve

fix.approach: Add a transactional reserveForward(intent) to the journal that fails if the hashlock or incoming (channelId, htlcId) already exists, and drive the forward path through it. Enforce uniqueness at the storage layer too.
constraints: Uniqueness must hold across processes, not only within one journal instance.
A retried forward must converge on the existing reservation, not create a second obligation.
Keep the existing journal shape readable for recovery.
acceptance: Concurrent forwards for one hashlock admit exactly one.
A duplicate reservation raises a typed conflict, not an overwrite.
Recovery sees the same association the forwarder committed.
verificationPostPublish: cd artifacts/canary && pnpm run canary run 38-omnia-relay-phase-a

findings.source: Omnia SDK audit — 25 November 2026, reporter finding OMN-083
findings.title: Forwarding compares amounts across assets without an exchange-rate authorization
findings.summary: The forward path rejects an outgoing amount greater than the incoming amount without first establishing that the two HTLCs are denominated in the same token. Comparing bare integers across different assets is not an economic check, and a cross-token forward has no authenticated rate at all.
findings.impact: A cross-token forward can be admitted on a meaningless numeric comparison, so the intermediary can pay out more value than it took in. Nothing in the journal records what rate was agreed.

repro.command: cd artifacts/canary && pnpm run canary run 15-omnia-cross-token-route
repro.expected: Same-asset forwarding requires matching token ids. A cross-asset hop requires an authenticated swap quote with explicit input/output amounts, assets, expiry and rate limits.
repro.actual: Two HTLCs with different token ids are compared by amount alone and the forward is admitted.

fix.approach: Require token equality for ordinary forwarding. Add an explicit cross-token branch that consumes a signed swap quote (input asset/amount, output asset/amount, rate, expiry, max slippage) and journals it with the link.
constraints: Never compare amounts across assets as a safety check.
A cross-token hop without a verified quote must be refused.
Journal the quote reference so recovery can re-check it.
acceptance: A same-asset forward with mismatched token ids is refused.
A cross-token forward without a verified quote is refused.
The journal records the rate and quote used.
verificationPostPublish: cd artifacts/canary && pnpm run canary run 15-omnia-cross-token-route

findings.source: Omnia SDK audit — 25 November 2026, reporter finding OMN-084
findings.title: An outgoing forward is journaled as active before the peer has received or acknowledged it
findings.summary: After signing the outgoing HTLC the forwarder writes the link with status 'active', then connects to the peer and sends STATE_UPDATE. The journal does not retain the exact signed proposal or a deterministic message id, so a transport failure leaves an obligation recorded as active that the counterparty has never seen.
findings.impact: Recovery cannot distinguish 'delivered and awaiting settlement' from 'never delivered'. The outgoing payment exists locally and may later be timed out on the intermediary's side, or be re-created with a different nonce, without any record of what the peer was actually offered.

repro.command: cd artifacts/canary && pnpm run canary run 38-omnia-relay-phase-a
repro.expected: The signed outgoing proposal is persisted with a deterministic message id and retransmitted until the peer acknowledges it.
repro.actual: The link is 'active' before connectToPeer/sendMessage, and neither the message nor an ack expectation is journaled.

fix.approach: Journal the exact signed state update and a deterministic message id as a delivery obligation before sending. Move to 'active' only after the peer acknowledges. Add acknowledgement-based retransmission to the recovery pass.
constraints: A link is not active until the peer has acknowledged it.
Retransmission must reuse the same signed message; never re-sign a new one.
Transport failure must leave a recoverable delivery obligation.
acceptance: A failed send leaves a pending-delivery record, not an active link.
Recovery retransmits the identical signed proposal.
A peer ack promotes the link to active exactly once.
verificationPostPublish: cd artifacts/canary && pnpm run canary run 38-omnia-relay-phase-a

findings.source: Omnia SDK audit — 25 November 2026, reporter finding OMN-085
findings.title: Exit entitlement verification checks that a pool epoch exists, not that it publishes this root
findings.summary: verifyVtxoExitEntitlement() compares the entitlement root with the VTXO's own proof root, then — when an authoritative pool is supplied — only checks that a pool.epochRoots entry exists for the entitlement's epoch number. The published root for that epoch is never compared, and the decoded payout output's token id is never checked against the entitlement token.
findings.impact: An entitlement can pass every local check while disagreeing with the authoritative pool's published commitment, depending entirely on the injected witness verifier. A payout in the wrong asset is accepted as long as the amount and address match.

repro.expected: Entitlement, decoded transaction, inclusion proof, published epoch root and payout token are bound to the same authoritative pool commitment.
repro.actual: A pool whose epochRoots lists the epoch with a different root still verifies, and a payout output in a different token passes.
evidence: packages/omnia-vtxo/src/exit-entitlement.ts:120-133 — payout address and amount, no token check

fix.approach: Resolve the published root for the entitlement epoch and require equality with the entitlement root. Compare the decoded payout token id with the entitlement token id. Require an inclusion proof for the entitlement leaf when a pool root is available.
constraints: Do not weaken the existing VTXO-local root comparison.
Historical epochs must verify against their own published root.
Fail closed when the authoritative pool does not publish the epoch.
acceptance: An epoch published with a different root fails verification.
A payout in the wrong token fails verification.
A correct entitlement in a historical epoch still verifies.
An unpublished epoch fails rather than being skipped.

findings.source: Omnia SDK audit — 25 November 2026, reporter finding OMN-086
findings.title: createExitDraft returns a receipt without consuming it
findings.summary: The doc comment says createExitDraft consumes the VTXO's receipt so a second exit draft is refused. The implementation checks exitConsumedAt, builds a draft and returns a receipt; consumption requires a separate consumeExitReceipt call that nothing forces.
findings.impact: Repeated calls generate competing exit drafts for the same VTXO. The underlying UTXO cannot be double-spent, so this is not a fund-loss path, but the SDK-level single-exit guarantee the API advertises does not hold, and callers that skip the second call get two drafts they may act on independently.

repro.expected: One call atomically reserves the exit against the authoritative VTXO store; a repeat returns the original draft.
repro.actual: createExitDraft can be called twice in a row against the same VTXO object and returns two receipts.
evidence: packages/omnia-vtxo/src/exit.ts:136-148 — consumeExitReceipt is a separate opt-in call

fix.approach: Make creation reserve the exit atomically (store-backed) and return the existing draft on a repeat request rather than a new one. Deprecate the two-step API or make the separate call a no-op once reserved.
constraints: Repeated requests must be idempotent, not error-and-forget.
Reservation must be durable across a restart.
Do not change the receipt id derivation for an existing draft.
acceptance: A second createExitDraft returns the first draft and receipt.
A VTXO with a reserved exit cannot produce a competing draft.
The reservation survives a restart.

findings.source: Omnia SDK audit — 25 November 2026, reporter finding OMN-087
findings.title: markExited accepts any non-empty transaction id as proof of exit
findings.summary: markExited() requires status 'exiting' and a non-empty txpowId, then records the VTXO as exited. It does not verify that the transaction exists, is confirmed, succeeds, or pays the correct owner the correct amount.
findings.impact: As an internal state reducer under a trusted caller this may be acceptable, but the exported API reads as completion of an exit. Any consumer treating 'exited' as verified settlement can be shown a fabricated exit.

repro.expected: Broadcast, confirmation and final settlement are distinct states, and the final transition requires authoritative chain evidence.
repro.actual: markExited(vtxo, { txpowId: 'x' }) yields status 'exited'.

fix.approach: Split the state machine: broadcast (tx id known), confirmed (buried), settled (verified payout). Require an injected chain witness for the confirmed and settled transitions, and rename the current function to make its trust level explicit.
constraints: Do not rename a trusted reducer into a verifier without adding the verification.
The final transition must be able to fail closed when the chain cannot be read.
Keep existing stored VTXOs readable.
acceptance: An unconfirmed or unknown transaction cannot reach the settled state.
The payout is verified against the expected owner and amount on the final transition.
The API distinguishes local bookkeeping from verified completion.

findings.source: Omnia SDK audit — 25 November 2026, reporter finding OMN-088
findings.title: Pool payout trusts caller-supplied position and intent instead of the registry
findings.summary: executePoolPayout() checks params.intent.status === 'approved' and verifies settlement evidence, then derives the accounting transition from params.position and params.intent directly. It never resolves the authoritative position or withdrawal intent from the registry it is given, and never compares them.
findings.impact: A stale or inconsistent position object can drive a new accounting transition: the payout can be computed against an amount, status or receipt that the registry has already superseded. Directly relevant to Pool 001, where LP capital accounting is the thing being protected.

repro.command: cd artifacts/canary && pnpm run canary run 24-omnia-pool-001-rehearsal
repro.expected: The payout resolves the position and intent from the registry, requires the caller's inputs to match, and binds the transition to the registry revision it consumed.
repro.actual: A position with an inflated amount is paid out without the registry being consulted.
evidence: no registry position lookup exists in the payout path

fix.approach: Load the position and intent from the registry by id, require them to match the supplied objects (or reject the supplied objects entirely), and carry the registry revision into the accounting update so a concurrent mutation is detected.
constraints: The registry is the only authority for position state.
A missing registry record is an error, not a reason to use the caller's copy.
The transition must be revision-bound so it cannot apply twice.
acceptance: A position that differs from the registry is refused.
A payout against a superseded intent is refused.
The accounting update records the registry revision consumed.
verificationPostPublish: cd artifacts/canary && pnpm run canary run 24-omnia-pool-001-rehearsal

findings.source: Omnia SDK audit — 25 November 2026, reporter finding OMN-089
findings.title: A partial withdrawal resets the remaining liquidity to fully available and unimpaired
findings.summary: After a payout the remaining position is written with effectiveAmount = availableAmount = remaining and allocatedAmount = reservedAmount = 0n. That asserts the residual capital has no outstanding allocations, no reservations and no impairment — none of which the payout established.
findings.impact: With residual obligations or impaired capital, the registry overstates immediately available liquidity, which is the number a withdrawal or Pool 001 capacity decision is made on.

repro.expected: Outstanding allocations and reservations are preserved or reduced by the withdrawn amount, and effective-value adjustments survive.
repro.actual: A position with allocatedAmount 5000 and a partial withdrawal comes back with allocatedAmount 0.

fix.approach: Reconcile instead of resetting: subtract the withdrawn amount from allocated/reserved in the position's own terms, keep the impairment adjustment, and refuse the payout if the withdrawal would strand an allocation that cannot be reduced.
constraints: Never raise available liquidity beyond what the pre-payout record justified.
Preserve the effective-value ratio across a partial withdrawal.
Refuse rather than guess when allocations exceed the remaining amount.
acceptance: A partial withdrawal preserves outstanding allocations.
An impaired position stays impaired after a partial withdrawal.
The available amount never increases because of a withdrawal.

findings.source: Omnia SDK audit — 25 November 2026, reporter finding OMN-090
findings.title: Liquidity receipt consumption is skipped when the receipt is missing
findings.summary: The payout consumes the liquidity receipt only if nextRegistry.receipts[position.receiptId] exists. For a position that names a receipt id, a missing receipt should be an integrity failure; instead the payout completes without consuming anything.
findings.impact: A receipt-backed position can be paid out while its receipt remains unconsumed, so the single-spend marker is silently bypassed. Whether that becomes a double withdrawal depends on other checks the audit cannot assume.

repro.expected: Every receipt-backed payout requires and atomically consumes the authoritative receipt; a missing one aborts the payout.
repro.actual: Deleting the receipt from the registry lets the payout succeed with no consumption.

fix.approach: Treat position.receiptId as mandatory for receipt-backed positions: resolve it, fail if absent, consume it in the same transition, and mint a successor receipt for the remaining balance on a partial withdrawal.
constraints: Fail closed on a missing receipt.
Consumption and accounting update must be one atomic transition.
A partial withdrawal must not leave the successor without a receipt.
acceptance: A receipt-backed payout with no receipt fails.
A consumed receipt cannot be consumed again.
A partial withdrawal produces a successor receipt for the remainder.

findings.source: Omnia SDK audit — 25 November 2026, reporter finding OMN-091
findings.title: Fulfilment and timeout are both eligible at the exact timeout block
findings.summary: fulfillHTLC() refuses only when tip.block > htlc.timeoutBlock; timeoutHTLC() refuses only when tip.block < htlc.timeoutBlock. At exactly timeoutBlock both transitions pass their SDK-level guard, so the two branches of the same HTLC overlap for one block.
findings.impact: Two parties can each believe their transition is valid at the same height. The on-chain script decides the real boundary, so the SDK can co-sign a state the deployed KISSVM contract rejects, or accept a conflicting claim it should have refused.

repro.command: cd artifacts/canary && pnpm run canary run 11-omnia-direct-channel
repro.expected: Exactly one transition is eligible at every height, matching the deployed script.
repro.actual: At tip.block == timeoutBlock both fulfillHTLC and timeoutHTLC proceed past their guards.

fix.approach: Adopt one canonical boundary rule that matches the deployed KISSVM comparison, expose it as a single shared predicate, and apply it in every package that reasons about HTLC expiry.
constraints: The rule must match the on-chain script exactly; derive it from the script, not from a preference.
Do not leave two implementations of the boundary.
Changing the boundary is a wire/behaviour change: note it in the changelog.
acceptance: At most one of fulfil/refund is eligible at any height.
The SDK boundary and the deployed script agree at the critical block.
One exported predicate is used everywhere the boundary is evaluated.
verificationPostPublish: cd artifacts/canary && pnpm run canary run 12-omnia-direct-settlement

findings.source: Omnia SDK audit — 25 November 2026, reporter finding OMN-092
findings.title: HTLC fulfilment receipts are not bound to the authenticated transition that paid them
findings.summary: The receipt builder reads amount and fulfilment status from the channel's historical HTLC records, and the verifier authenticates a supplied signed state with the recipient's signature. Neither establishes that the specific transition from the preceding authenticated state fulfilled that HTLC and moved the stated amount.
findings.impact: Receipt verification cannot stand alone as a financial earn-proof boundary. A receipt can be produced for an amount the transition did not actually transfer, which undermines the pool fee accounting that consumes it (see OMN-083).

repro.expected: Verification checks the authenticated predecessor and successor states, the HTLC identity, the preimage commitment, the exact balance delta and both parties' authorization.
repro.actual: A receipt whose amount differs from the state delta still verifies against a validly signed successor state.
evidence: amount and status sourced from channel.pendingHTLCs, not from the state delta

fix.approach: Carry the predecessor and successor state hashes in the receipt, derive the amount from the balance delta between them, include the hashlock/preimage commitment and both signatures, and verify all of it.
constraints: Do not trust the historical HTLC record for the amount.
Version the receipt format; old receipts must not silently pass the new verifier.
Verification must fail closed when the predecessor state is unavailable.
acceptance: A receipt whose amount does not match the state delta fails.
A receipt for an HTLC absent from the transition fails.
A missing counterparty signature fails.
Downstream fee accounting refuses an unverified receipt.

findings.source: Omnia SDK audit — 25 November 2026, reporter finding OMN-093
findings.title: A factory participant's latest off-chain allocation is not unilaterally enforceable
findings.summary: The OMN-058 work added an output-enforced distribution branch that reads every share from PREVSTATE and pins destinations, amounts, output count and conservation. But checkpoint enforcement is still optional at the script-builder level, and the distribution implementation states that it covers the latest confirmed allocation only. A newer off-chain allocation therefore has no enforceable on-chain artifact.
findings.impact: A participant's economic entitlement can differ from what they can unilaterally take on chain. This is a capability boundary rather than a regression: there are two distinct production modes and only one of them is enforceable. Treating OMN-058 as fully closed overstates the guarantee.

repro.command: cd artifacts/canary && pnpm run canary run 16-omnia-factory
repro.expected: The enforceable on-chain entitlement always equals the participant's latest valid allocation, including an off-chain update that no one has checkpointed.
repro.actual: With enforceCheckpoints off, an off-chain allocation change is not represented on chain. With it on, VC open/close and reallocate are refused until the change is checkpointed.
evidence: packages/omnia-factory/src/script.ts:329-330 — enforceCheckpoints is optional, off by default
packages/omnia-factory/src/distribution.ts:1-12 — scope is the latest confirmed allocation

fix.approach: Keep this as a documented release restriction with two named modes: 'confirmed checkpoint factory' (latest confirmed allocation, enforceable) and 'fully off-chain contestable factory' (latest valid off-chain allocation, outstanding). Do not advertise the second until the contest protocol lands.
constraints: Do not describe the factory as fully off-chain-enforceable in docs or manifests.
Do not close OMN-058 on the strength of the checkpoint branch alone.
Refuse off-chain allocation changes on a non-checkpointed factory rather than allowing an unenforceable state.
acceptance: The capability claim distinguishes the two factory modes.
A non-checkpointed factory cannot accumulate an unenforceable allocation delta.
The limitation is recorded in the RFC and the register rather than only in a code comment.
verificationPostPublish: cd artifacts/canary && pnpm run canary run 16-omnia-factory

findings.title: Channel activation conflates funding depth with peer acceptance
findings.source: Omnia adversarial audit — 26 November 2026, reporter finding OMN-097 (omnia-host/src/api/methods.ts:1351-1368, 1380-1414, 2814-2838)
findings.summary: The read path promotes funding_pending and opening channels to active on funding depth alone, while resubmitChannelProposal promotes on acknowledgement without rechecking depth. Each condition is necessary but neither is sufficient.
findings.impact: A channel can be advertised active with no counterparty record, or with an unconfirmed funding coin. Routing and payment then act on a channel that cannot settle.

repro.expected: Activation requires funding depth, an authenticated acknowledgement, and a persisted initial exit package.
repro.actual: Activation depends on whichever condition the caller last observed.

fix.approach: Introduce one activation gate that requires all conditions and is the only path to active.
constraints: Keep pending states readable and recoverable.
Do not make the ACK authoritative for on-chain state.
acceptance: A funded channel with no ACK is not active.
An ACK without depth is not active.
Activation is idempotent.

findings.title: Unilateral update coin verification does not bind sequence, commitment, amount or lineage
findings.source: Omnia adversarial audit — 26 November 2026, reporter finding OMN-098 (omnia/src/settlement.ts:490-532)
findings.summary: recordUnilateralUpdateCoin verifies the coin exists, is unspent, sits at the expected address and reaches a confirmation depth, then uses its creation height for the contest deadline. It does not check the coin's sequence, state commitment, amount/token or the transaction that produced it.
findings.impact: A coin that merely looks right can set the contest deadline, so a dispute can be timed against an unrelated coin. Same class as the splice successor finding; it needs one shared lineage verifier.

repro.expected: The update coin is bound to the expected sequence, commitment, amount, token and creating transaction.
repro.actual: Only spent/address/depth are checked.
evidence: no sequence/commitment comparison in the function

fix.approach: Use the shared channel-lineage verifier (transaction body + predecessor consumption + successor state) before accepting the contest deadline.
constraints: Do not duplicate lineage logic per package.
Fail closed when the chain cannot return the transaction.
acceptance: A coin with the wrong sequence or commitment is rejected.
The deadline derives only from a verified successor.

findings.title: A unilateral settlement broadcast is recorded as a completed closure
findings.source: Omnia adversarial audit — 26 November 2026, reporter finding OMN-099 (omnia/src/settlement.ts:589-622)
findings.summary: finalizeUnilateralClose broadcasts the settlement transaction and immediately calls markChannelClosed. Nothing verifies inclusion in the canonical chain, so an accepted-but-unconfirmed transaction yields a closed channel.
findings.impact: The application reports closure and may stop watching while the transaction is absent or reorged, leaving funds in a state nobody monitors.

repro.expected: Broadcast, confirmation and final closure are distinct states; closure requires chain evidence.
repro.actual: markChannelClosed follows the broadcast directly.

fix.approach: Split the lifecycle into closing_unilateral → settlement_broadcast → settlement_confirmed → closed, with an injected chain verifier for the final transition.
constraints: Do not mark closed without confirmation.
Keep the broadcast id recoverable.
acceptance: An unconfirmed settlement is not closed.
A reorg reopens monitoring.
Closure requires verified inclusion.

findings.title: The distributed multi-hop branch bypasses the durable operation lifecycle
findings.source: Omnia adversarial audit — 26 November 2026, reporter finding OMN-100 (omnia-host/src/api/methods.ts:4085-4146)
findings.summary: The distributed payment branch creates an HTLC, persists the channel and sends the message, returning before the withOperation wrapper used by the local branch. It reports first-hop-accepted after sending without an explicit acknowledgement.
findings.impact: Distributed payments lack the operation journal, idempotency and unknown-outcome handling added for local execution, and can report acceptance the peer never gave.

repro.expected: Every payment path uses the same durable execution lifecycle.
repro.actual: The distributed branch returns outside withOperation.

fix.approach: Route the distributed branch through withOperation with an operation id, persist the signed proposal, wait for acknowledgement and record refund obligations.
constraints: Do not require a local channel for the distributed path.
Reuse the relay delivery journal for retransmission.
acceptance: A retried distributed payment is idempotent.
Acceptance is reported only after acknowledgement.
Undelivered proposals are recoverable.

findings.title: Cross-token locality is decided from the inbound channel only
findings.source: Omnia adversarial audit — 26 November 2026, reporter finding OMN-101 (omnia-host/src/api/methods.ts:4077-4092)
findings.summary: The host decides whether every hop is local from each hop's channelId. A swap hop carries inboundChannelId and outboundChannelId; the lease map handles both, but the locality check does not verify that the outbound side is local. The reporter corrected the earlier claim that swap hops lack channelId.
findings.impact: A route in which both channels are local can be classified distributed and rejected by the unsupported-distributed-swap guard.

repro.expected: Locality covers both sides of a swap hop.
repro.actual: Only the inbound side is considered.

fix.approach: Check inboundChannelId and outboundChannelId for swap hops when deciding locality.
constraints: Do not treat a partial swap as local.
Keep the lease map construction unchanged.
acceptance: A fully local cross-token route executes.
A route with a remote outbound side is classified distributed.

findings.title: The S4 harness can report S4_PASS without asserting settlement
findings.source: Omnia adversarial audit — 26 November 2026, reporter finding OMN-102 (scripts/omnia-s4-cross.mjs:207-246)
findings.summary: The harness logs the settlement and close responses and then constructs a result with pass: true. It does not assert that settlement and closure succeeded or that the expected payout outputs exist on chain, so an RPC response containing a logical failure can reach S4_PASS.
findings.impact: The automatic pass indicator cannot be relied on as evidence. The documented on-chain outputs from the 25 November run stand; the harness result alone does not prove them.

repro.expected: PASS requires balance conservation, expected recipient balances, matching peer sequences and confirmed closure.
repro.actual: pass: true is constructed after logging.

fix.approach: Assert the final invariants before printing S4_PASS: conservation, recipient balances, sequences, settlement outputs, predecessor consumption and closure on both hosts.
constraints: Do not weaken existing assertions.
Keep the harness usable without live infrastructure (skip, not pass).
acceptance: A logical failure in any step yields a non-zero exit.
S4_PASS implies every asserted invariant held.

findings.title: Automated watcher actions bypass the channel mutation coordinator
findings.source: Omnia adversarial audit — 26 November 2026, reporter finding OMN-103 (omnia-host/src/watch.ts:163-205, lifecycle.ts:1194-1289)
findings.summary: The watch service executes settlement and HTLC timeout actions and writes the resulting channel state without acquiring the shared per-channel lock used by RPC and peer-message handlers. Its interval has no in-flight guard.
findings.impact: A watcher action can interleave with an operator or peer-driven mutation on the same channel, producing concurrent state writes.

repro.expected: Watcher actions take the same channel lock and reload state after acquiring it; scans are single-flight.
repro.actual: Scans were unsynchronised and the action path did not take the lock.

fix.approach: Route watcher actions through the channel coordinator, reload authoritative state, and single-flight scans.
constraints: Do not deadlock with RPC callers.
Leave findings unprocessed on lock contention so the next pass retries.
acceptance: A watcher action cannot run concurrently with an RPC mutation of the same channel.
Scans never overlap.

origin.note: reporter id OMN-103; Scan single-flight landed with OMN-096; the action-path lock remains open.

findings.title: Epoch recovery reconstructs history without authenticating it
findings.source: Omnia adversarial audit — 26 November 2026, reporter finding OMN-105 (vtxo/src/epoch-authority.ts:64-83)
findings.summary: Recovery rebuilds spent inputs and the current root from journal entries by taking the highest epoch. It does not verify each epoch signature, reject conflicting roots at one epoch, enforce transition ordering or detect repeated input consumption.
findings.impact: Structural recovery is relied on as financial recovery; a corrupted journal can restore a root the operator never signed.

repro.expected: Replay verifies signatures, monotonic epochs, unique inputs and agreement with the anchored epoch.
repro.actual: Recovery trusts the highest recorded epoch.

fix.approach: Authenticated deterministic replay with monotonic validation and reconciliation against the externally anchored epoch.
constraints: Fail closed on a signature that does not verify.
Reject conflicting roots at the same epoch.
acceptance: A tampered journal entry cannot restore state.
Recovery matches the anchored epoch.

findings.title: An interrupted signer response can release the signing guard
findings.source: Omnia adversarial audit — 26 November 2026, reporter finding OMN-107 (omnia/src/sign.ts:323-354)
findings.summary: The signing guard is sealed only after the signer returns. If an external signer produces a signature but the response is lost, the failure path abandons the attempt and releases the guard even though a signature may exist.
findings.impact: Remote and asynchronous signers can be asked to sign twice at one sequence after a timeout.

repro.expected: An uncertain signing outcome stays locked until reconciled.
repro.actual: A thrown or timed-out signer is treated as "no signature".

fix.approach: Distinguish a definite signer refusal from an unknown outcome; keep the guard sealed for the latter and require reconciliation.
constraints: Do not treat a transport timeout as a refusal.
Keep a definite pre-sign refusal retryable.
acceptance: A timed-out signer leaves the attempt sealed.
Reconciliation can commit or abandon it explicitly.

findings.title: Allocation verification ignores reserved and risk-adjusted capital
findings.source: Omnia adversarial audit — 26 November 2026, reporter finding OMN-110 (liquidity-bond/src/allocation.ts:34-47)
findings.summary: Available liquidity is computed as amount minus allocatedAmount. Reserved capital and the effective (risk-adjusted) amount are ignored, and allocatePositionCapital executes the channel or factory operation before checking whether the position is now overallocated.
findings.impact: Capital can be committed beyond what the position can actually support; the check reports the overcommitment after execution.

repro.expected: Availability subtracts allocated and reserved, and is capped by effective value before execution.
repro.actual: Only allocatedAmount is subtracted, after execution.

fix.approach: Compute headroom from effective minus allocated minus reserved before executing, and refuse the operation when it would overcommit.
constraints: Do not add a post-hoc check in place of a pre-execution one.
Preserve existing allocation bookkeeping.
acceptance: An allocation exceeding risk-adjusted headroom is refused before any channel operation.
Reserved capital reduces availability.

findings.title: The recorded allocation amount is not bound to the executed operation
findings.source: Omnia adversarial audit — 26 November 2026, reporter finding OMN-111 (omnia-pool/src/allocate.ts:87-156)
findings.summary: The registry amount comes from params.amount while the channel, factory or VTXO operation receives separate target parameters. Nothing verifies that the executed operation deployed the same amount, asset and ownership allocation.
findings.impact: The registry can record an allocation that differs from what was actually deployed.

repro.expected: Execution parameters are derived from the authorized allocation.
repro.actual: Accounting amount and execution target are independent inputs.

fix.approach: Derive the execution target from the allocation record; verify the resulting deployment before registering it.
constraints: One source of truth for the amount.
Do not trust caller-supplied target amounts.
acceptance: A mismatched execution target is refused.
The recorded amount equals the deployed amount.

findings.title: An allocation can be released without proof of capital recovery
findings.source: Omnia adversarial audit — 26 November 2026, reporter finding OMN-112 (omnia-pool/src/allocate.ts:198-229)
findings.summary: releaseAllocation marks the allocation released and restores available liquidity by accounting only. It does not verify that the channel settled, the factory allocation was recovered or obligations were discharged.
findings.impact: Released accounting is treated as recovered capital, so liquidity can be redeployed while the funds are still committed.

repro.expected: Release requires evidence of recovery; the registry distinguishes releasing, pending settlement and recovered.
repro.actual: Release is an accounting operation.

fix.approach: Add a settlement-evidence gate to release and a pending-settlement state that does not count as available.
constraints: Do not count pending settlement as available liquidity.
Keep the release recoverable after a restart.
acceptance: A release without recovered capital is refused or parked.
Availability only increases after verified recovery.

findings.title: Factory persistence permits a stale record to overwrite a newer one
findings.source: Omnia adversarial audit — 26 November 2026, reporter finding OMN-113 (omnia-factory/src/durable-factory-store.ts:83-88)
findings.summary: saveFactory replaces the whole record without comparing the incoming sequence with the stored sequence. The storage CAS protects the write, not the semantic ordering of factory state.
findings.impact: A delayed writer can roll a factory back to an older allocation or sequence.

repro.expected: Writes are rejected when the incoming sequence is below the stored sequence.
repro.actual: Whole-record replace.

fix.approach: Enforce monotonic sequence at the store boundary and fail the write on regression.
constraints: Do not require callers to pre-check the sequence.
Keep recovery able to read older records.
acceptance: A stale save is rejected.
Concurrent writers converge on the highest sequence.

findings.title: Splice acceptance can regress a finalized record
findings.source: Omnia adversarial audit — 26 November 2026, reporter finding OMN-114 (omnia-splice/src/durable-splice-store.ts:122-145)
findings.summary: saveAcceptance sets the record status to accepted without checking the current status, so a delayed or replayed acceptance can overwrite a record already marked finalized.
findings.impact: Recovery can re-enter the finalize path for an already-finalized splice.

repro.expected: Splice records follow a monotonic state machine and acceptances are immutable once bound.
repro.actual: saveAcceptance writes accepted unconditionally.

fix.approach: Add a monotonic transition table and reject acceptance once finalized.
constraints: Keep pending→accepted→finalized ordering.
Do not accept a different acceptance for the same splice.
acceptance: A replayed acceptance cannot regress finalized.
A conflicting acceptance is rejected.

findings.title: VTXO split outputs can receive duplicate identifiers
findings.source: Omnia adversarial audit — 26 November 2026, reporter finding OMN-115 (vtxo/src/split.ts:24-53)
findings.summary: splitVtxo checks that the amount and nonce arrays have equal length but not that output ids are unique. Splitting into equal amounts with identical nonces produces identical ids, and the proof map is keyed by id.
findings.impact: Output records can overwrite each other or become ambiguous.

repro.expected: Every split output identifier is unique within the batch.
repro.actual: Uniqueness is not enforced.

fix.approach: Reject duplicate output ids in split (the invariant OMN-046 applied to refresh).
constraints: Apply the same invariant to every VTXO transformation.
Do not silently rename outputs.
acceptance: A split with duplicate ids is refused.
Merge/refresh/split share the uniqueness guard.

findings.title: VTXO conservation verification accepts duplicate and negative records
findings.source: Omnia adversarial audit — 26 November 2026, reporter finding OMN-116 (vtxo/src/verify.ts:241-293)
findings.summary: verifyConservation checks pool ids, token ids and aggregate amounts. It does not reject duplicate inputs, duplicate outputs or individually negative records.
findings.impact: A crafted input set can pass conservation while double-counting or negating amounts.

repro.expected: Duplicate ids and negative amounts are rejected centrally.
repro.actual: Only aggregates are compared.

fix.approach: Add duplicate-id and non-negative checks to the shared verifier.
constraints: Keep the strict/lte modes.
Do not rely on per-caller guards.
acceptance: Duplicate inputs or outputs fail.
A negative amount fails.

findings.title: A malformed routing envelope is interpreted as a final destination
findings.source: Omnia adversarial audit — 26 November 2026, reporter finding OMN-117 (omnia-router/src/forward.ts:75-94)
findings.summary: decode catches JSON parse failures and returns kind final, treating malformed input as an instruction that this node is the recipient.
findings.impact: A corrupted or hostile envelope can turn an intermediary into the recipient of a payment it did not earn.

repro.expected: Malformed input produces an invalid-envelope error.
repro.actual: Parse failure becomes final.

fix.approach: Return a distinct invalid-envelope result and make callers refuse it.
constraints: Keep a genuinely final hop working.
Do not let the resolver fulfil on an invalid envelope.
acceptance: Malformed input is rejected.
A final hop still settles.

findings.title: Routing advertisements include channels that are not active
findings.source: Omnia adversarial audit — 26 November 2026, reporter finding OMN-118 (omnia-relay/src/routing.ts:58-89)
findings.summary: The routing graph excludes only closed channels, so opening, funding-pending, disputing and closing channels appear as usable edges.
findings.impact: Routes can be computed through channels that cannot carry a payment.

repro.expected: Only active, verified, unencumbered channels are advertised.
repro.actual: Everything except closed.

fix.approach: Require an active status allow-list plus funding verification.
constraints: Do not advertise a channel before activation.
Keep peers able to learn the channel exists without routing it.
acceptance: Non-active channels are not routable.
A closing channel is withdrawn promptly.

findings.title: The signing policy is skipped when a request carries no amount
findings.source: Omnia adversarial audit — 26 November 2026, reporter finding OMN-119 (omnia-host/src/signer-port.ts:153-168, omnia/src/sign.ts:277-288)
findings.summary: The policy signer applies its maximum-amount check only when request.context.amount is supplied. signState constructs chain-signing requests without an amount, so a configured spending limit does not apply to them.
findings.impact: A spending policy can be bypassed by a signing path that omits the amount.

repro.expected: Policy inputs derive from the canonical transaction and the channel transition.
repro.actual: Amount is optional caller metadata.

fix.approach: Derive the amount from the transaction being signed and refuse when it cannot be determined.
constraints: Do not make the limit optional.
Keep non-financial signing paths working.
acceptance: A request without a derivable amount is refused under a spending policy.
The limit uses the canonical amount.

findings.title: The Axia lease adapter does not defensively validate remote indices
findings.source: Omnia adversarial audit — 26 November 2026, reporter finding OMN-120 (wots-lease/src/omnia-axia.ts:117-158)
findings.summary: The adapter defaults missing returned indices to zero and checks the watermark with the supplied logical tree id, without establishing a local atomic reservation over the cryptographic key domain before returning the lease.
findings.impact: An incomplete or conflicting remote response can be used as a lease, risking WOTS leaf reuse if the remote guarantee does not hold.

repro.expected: Incomplete or conflicting lease responses are rejected locally.
repro.actual: Missing indices default to zero.

fix.approach: Reject responses missing any index, verify they advance the local watermark, and record a local reservation.
constraints: Fail closed on a partial lease.
Keep the remote contract as documented.
acceptance: A response without indices fails.
A conflicting lease fails.
A local reservation exists before use.

findings.title: Journal recovery can race an in-progress append
findings.source: Omnia adversarial audit — 26 November 2026, reporter finding OMN-121 (storage/src/journal.ts:250-287, 325-350)
findings.summary: The journal advances its head before writing the entry, so recovery can read the missing entry as an interrupted append and roll the head backwards while another writer is mid-append. No lock spans recovery and an independent writer.
findings.impact: Concurrent recovery and append can lose or duplicate journal entries that other packages rely on for crash safety.

repro.expected: Append and recovery are mutually exclusive.
repro.actual: Recovery can roll the head back under a live writer.

fix.approach: Take an exclusive lock across recovery and appends, and only truncate entries proven abandoned.
constraints: Do not lose a committed entry.
Keep single-writer performance.
acceptance: Recovery during a paused append converges.
A cross-process regression test covers the race.

findings.title: Confirmation depth is computed differently across packages
findings.source: Omnia adversarial audit — 26 November 2026, reporter finding OMN-122 (chain-provider/src/verify-deposit.ts:52-85, omnia/src/chain-truth.ts:29-37)
findings.summary: Omnia computes depth as tip minus creation height; the deposit verifier computes tip minus creation height plus one, and also treats a positive MMR entry as confirmation. Two packages can disagree about the same coin reaching a threshold.
findings.impact: The same coin can be confirmed for one purpose and unconfirmed for another, so activation and deposit gates disagree.

repro.expected: One shared confirmation definition.
repro.actual: Two definitions with a one-block offset.

fix.approach: Export one confirmation helper from chain-provider and use it everywhere.
constraints: Keep the conservative definition.
Do not change activation semantics silently.
acceptance: All packages agree at the boundary block.
Boundary tests cover tip == created and tip == created + n.

findings.title: Fee earn-proofs can be appended more than once
findings.source: Omnia adversarial audit — 26 November 2026, reporter finding OMN-123 (omnia-pool/src/fees.ts:41-77, liquidity-bond/src/registry.ts:98-106)
findings.summary: recordPoolFee verifies earn-proof evidence and appends a fee record; the registry appends without enforcing uniqueness of the evidence. The payout side has replay controls, the earning side does not.
findings.impact: Repeated submission of the same valid evidence inflates recorded earned fees.

repro.expected: Evidence is consumed exactly once.
repro.actual: Append-only with no evidence key.

fix.approach: Key fee records by evidence digest and reject a duplicate.
constraints: Do not change the fee record shape without versioning.
Keep legitimate multiple fees per hop distinct.
acceptance: The same evidence twice records one fee.
Distinct evidence still records.

findings.title: The TxPoW work verifier fails open when parsing fails
findings.source: Omnia adversarial audit — 26 November 2026, reporter finding OMN-124 (txpow/src/verify.ts:234-265)
findings.summary: When the parser cannot establish the TxPoW structure, verifyTxPoWWork hashes the raw bytes as a proxy identifier and evaluates it against a floor difficulty, so the result can be valid for input that is not a TxPoW.
findings.impact: Any admission or relay path that relies on this result can accept a malformed payload.

repro.expected: A structural parse failure returns valid: false on the authoritative path.
repro.actual: A fallback hash can satisfy the floor.

fix.approach: Return invalid on parse failure; keep any lenient behaviour behind an explicit opt-in.
constraints: Do not let a fallback produce validity.
Keep diagnostics available.
acceptance: Malformed input is invalid.
A well-formed TxPoW still verifies.

findings.title: Virtual-channel planning accepts the same participant twice
findings.source: Omnia adversarial audit — 26 November 2026, reporter finding OMN-125 (omnia-factory/src/virtual.ts:114-168)
findings.summary: buildVirtualChannelOpen checks that both supplied participants exist but not that they differ. Identical ids make both allocation deductions target one key, so one assignment overwrites the other.
findings.impact: A malformed plan can produce a commitment with a self-referential allocation.

repro.expected: The planner rejects duplicate participants before producing a commitment.
repro.actual: Distinctness is not checked.

fix.approach: Reject identical party ids before any allocation mutation or signing.
constraints: Keep the downstream script guard as defence in depth.
Do not produce a commitment on a rejected plan.
acceptance: Identical participants are rejected.
A valid pair still plans.

findings.title: The initiator discards the peer ERROR frame, so a rejected open reports only acknowledged=false
findings.source: live runs: omnia-open-noncustodial.mjs against Hawk v0.2.12 and v0.3.0
findings.summary: The wire protocol defines an ERROR message carrying payload.error, and the responder sends it with a precise reason. requestPeerReply does receive it, but submitOpenChannel reduces the reply to acknowledged = reply.type === 'ACK' and drops the payload; the integration router has no ERROR branch at all, so the frame is not surfaced anywhere.
findings.impact: Every peer-side rejection is opaque to the caller and to the operator log. In this run the actual cause (funding coin not on chain) only became visible after instrumenting the stream layer on the initiator. Support and automation cannot distinguish a rejected proposal from a lost one without patching the SDK.

repro.expected: The submit result or an observation record carries the responder's reason.
repro.actual: Submit returns { success: true, acknowledged: false } with no reason; nothing is logged unless OMNIA_DEBUG is on, and even then only "[omnia-stream] recv ERROR" with no payload.
evidence: packages/omnia/src/integration.ts: _sendError sends payload { error: reason } from 10 call sites
packages/omnia/src/integration.ts: the inbound router switches on CHANNEL_PROPOSAL/STATE_UPDATE/... but has no ERROR case
packages/omnia/src/stream.ts: debug logging prints the message type only
temporary logging-only instrumentation showed: {"error":"acceptChannel failed: Error: Funding coin 0x68778de3... not found on chain"}

fix.approach: Preserve the reason end to end: return it on the submit result (for example acknowledged:false with peerError), include it in the operation record and the observation stream, and handle ERROR explicitly in the integration router so first-contact and routed messages both surface the payload.
constraints: Do not change the ERROR wire format or the reply-matching rules (channelId + nonce).
Do not turn a rejection into a thrown exception where callers already branch on acknowledged.
Do not log secrets from the payload; the reason is a short string.
acceptance: A rejected proposal yields the responder reason to the caller and in the observation record.
The canary can assert on the reason without instrumenting node_modules.

findings.title: Splice successor selection matches on address, token and amount only
findings.source: security audit OMN-NEW-006, verified against source at 8fa26907
findings.summary: observeSpliceSuccessor picks the first unspent coin whose address, token and amount match. Nothing binds the candidate to the splice transaction that created it or to the expected state transition, and the first match wins rather than treating ambiguity as an error.
findings.impact: Two same-value coins at the same script address (a common shape for channel funding addresses) can make the host adopt the wrong coin as the spliced channel. Downstream operations then reference a coin the channel does not control.

repro.expected: The successor is identified by provenance (txid/output index) or ambiguity is rejected.
repro.actual: coins.find(...) on address+token+amount returns the first candidate.
evidence: fix proposed in PR #218 (ambiguous successor is an error)
packages/omnia-splice/src/successor.ts:83 — const candidate = coins.find((coin) => !coin.spent && address && tokenid && amount)

fix.approach: Accept an expected txid/output reference derived from the splice transaction, or read the successor from the spends of the predecessor coin. If more than one candidate matches, fail as ambiguous instead of choosing.
constraints: Do not silently pick a candidate when several match.
Keep the bounded polling and confirmation semantics.
acceptance: Duplicate same-value coins at the address produce an ambiguity error, not a silent pick.
The correct successor is still found in the single-candidate case.

findings.title: Router rollback cannot release HTLCs early and reports failure as if liquidity were returned
findings.source: security audit OMN-NEW-009, verified against source at 8fa26907
findings.summary: On a failed multi-hop payment the router calls timeoutHTLC on each still-pending lock and swallows every error. timeoutHTLC deliberately throws while the chain tip is below the HTLC timeout block, which is the normal case for a payment that just failed. So the rollback releases nothing, yet the failure result and the in-code comment ("stranded HTLCs are never left behind silently") imply it did.
findings.impact: Liquidity stays locked until the timeout block, and callers have no state that says so. A retry can fail for lack of capacity that is not actually gone. This is a recovery-state and API-contract defect, not direct fund theft.

repro.expected: A failed payment records explicit refund-pending locks and releases them once the timeout is valid.
repro.actual: cancelHtlcs catches and ignores the "has not yet timed out" error; the caller sees only a failure.
evidence: fix proposed in PR #218 (pendingRefunds on failure; cancelPayment throws PendingRefundError)
packages/omnia-router/src/execute.ts:52 — try { await ops.timeoutHTLC(...) } catch { /* best-effort */ }
packages/omnia-router/src/execute.ts:68 — comment claims stranded HTLCs are never left behind

fix.approach: Persist refund-pending locks with their timeout blocks, expose that state in the payment result, and retry when the timeout becomes valid. Distinguish refunded from refund-pending rather than collapsing both into a generic failure.
constraints: Do not claim liquidity was released when timeoutHTLC threw.
Do not bypass the timeout guard to force an early release.
acceptance: A failed payment reports which locks remain pending and until which block.
A retry after the timeout block releases them.
The success path is unchanged.

findings.title: Relay link journal is not atomic and duplicate detection races the write
findings.source: security audit OMN-NEW-010, verified against source at 8fa26907
findings.summary: record() writes the link, then reads the index, then writes the index as a separate operation with no transaction or compare-and-swap. Two concurrent forwards for the same hashlock both pass the duplicate check (which runs before record) and can then both record, with the second index write overwriting the first.
findings.impact: A lost index update hides a link from list()-based recovery, and a duplicate forward creates two outgoing HTLCs for one incoming payment. Both are restart-sensitive and hard to see in logs.

repro.expected: Journal writes are atomic and an incoming HTLC has a single idempotency key.
repro.actual: Two sequential storage.set calls per record; duplicate check precedes the write.
evidence: fix proposed in PR #218 (single-document journal, serialized, upsert by hashlock)

fix.approach: Use one atomic write per link (store the index inside the record, or use a storage transaction), and key idempotency on inChannelId+inHtlcId with a conditional insert. Recover from authoritative records, not from a separately maintained index.
constraints: Do not require a storage adapter feature the published adapters do not have.
Keep list() working for adapters that already hold data.
acceptance: Concurrent record() calls for the same hashlock produce exactly one entry and one outgoing HTLC.
A crash between the two writes cannot lose the link.

findings.title: Funding change goes to the first input owner, and the builder accepts negative output amounts
findings.source: security audit OMN-NEW-011, verified against source at 8fa26907
findings.summary: The CAN-001 fix returns change correctly for a single-owner coin, but two edges remain. With several funding inputs, all excess value is sent to inputAddresses[0] even when the inputs belong to different addresses. In tx-builder, amounts are summed per token and checked against the inputs, but individual negative amounts are never rejected, so a negative output can offset a positive one and still balance.
findings.impact: Multi-owner funding pays the change to the wrong party (and the transaction then cannot be signed by that party alone, so it fails late). The negative-amount gap means a draft can carry an invalid coin amount through conservation checking. Node acceptance of such a transaction was not demonstrated.

repro.expected: Change is returned per input owner, and every amount is required to be a non-negative integer before conservation is evaluated.
repro.actual: Change uses inputAddresses[0] unconditionally; sums() accepts BigInt("-100") and only compares totals.
evidence: fix proposed in PR #218 (mixed-owner funding rejected; negative amounts refused)
packages/tx-builder/src/build.ts:119 — sums() parses amounts with BigInt without a sign check
packages/tx-builder/src/build.ts:136 — only total > available is rejected

fix.approach: Require all funding inputs to share an owner before emitting change, or emit one change output per input address and reject mixed-owner funding with a clear error. In the builder, reject any amount that is negative or not an integer before summing.
constraints: Keep the single-input exact-value path byte-identical.
Do not weaken the existing conservation check.

findings.title: Prepared operations bypass the channel lock; refunds are not surfaced by the host; journal is not cross-process safe
findings.source: re-audit R-005, verified against source at 5d8c427b
findings.summary: Three related gaps remain. (1) The shared lock keys on params.channelId, so prepared operations that identify the work by preparedOperationId do not take it (and multi-channel work has no ordered locking). (2) The router now returns pendingRefunds, but the host multi-hop method throws on failure instead of returning that recovery information, and nothing persists a refund queue. (3) The relay journal is a single document per process, but has no storage-level compare-and-swap and does not serialize by incoming HTLC identity.
findings.impact: Concurrent prepared operations can interleave with RPC/peer mutations on the same channel; a failed multi-hop payment loses the refund schedule at the host boundary; two relay processes can lose a journal update.

repro.expected: Prepared, RPC and peer mutations share one lock; failures carry refunds; journal writes are atomic across processes.
repro.actual: Lock lookup ignores preparedOperationId; host throws the router result away; journal has no CAS.
evidence: packages/omnia-host/src/api/methods.ts:3342-3358 — lock key derived only from params.channelId
packages/omnia-router/src/execute.ts — pendingRefunds returned to the caller
packages/omnia-host/src/api/methods.ts — multi-hop handler throws without surfacing pendingRefunds
packages/omnia-relay/src/link-journal.ts — single document, no CAS or per-incoming-key lock

fix.approach: Resolve the channel from the prepared operation before taking the lock; sort multi-channel locks by channelId to avoid deadlock; return pendingRefunds from the host multi-hop method and persist a refund queue; add a compare-and-swap to the journal (revision field) and an idempotency key on inChannelId+inHtlcId.
constraints: Do not serialize unrelated channels.
Do not report a failure as fully refunded.
acceptance: A prepared submission and an RPC call on one channel cannot interleave.
Host multi-hop failures carry pendingRefunds and a scheduled retry.
Concurrent journal writers cannot lose an update.

findings.title: EpochAuthority.append is check-then-act across an await
findings.source: Omnia whole-family re-audit (2026-11-17), finding OMN-009
findings.summary: append() reads current state, checks `spentInputIds`, then awaits `journal.append`. Two concurrent appends for the same input can both pass the check before either writes.

repro.actual: Both can pass the spent-input check before either append lands.

acceptance: Two concurrent appends of the same input: one wins, one throws.

acceptance: Two hosts at different tips derive the same funding script from one proposal.

findings.source: Omnia SDK audit — 25 November 2026, reporter finding OMN-071
findings.title: Decimal parsing in the LSP truncates precision and mis-signs negative input
findings.summary: decimalKey() splits on '.', multiplies the whole part by 10^18 and adds the fraction padded or sliced to 18 digits. Fractional precision beyond 18 places is silently truncated, a negative value adds a positive fraction to a negative whole (so -1.5 parses as -0.5), and malformed or empty parts reach BigInt() and throw. The same function is duplicated in quote.ts, so the two copies can drift.

repro.actual: decimalKey('-1.5') yields -500000000000000000n; '1.0000000000000000001' truncates to 1; 'abc' throws SyntaxError from BigInt.

fix.approach: Replace both copies with one strict parser in @totemsdk/omnia-lsp: /^(0|[1-9][0-9]*)(\.[0-9]+)?$/, reject negative values, reject excess precision instead of truncating, and return a discriminated result rather than throwing.
constraints: One implementation, shared by policy, quote and any future fee code.
Do not silently round: excess precision is a rejection.
Keep the on-wire decimal string format unchanged.
acceptance: Negative, malformed and over-precise amounts are refused with a policy error.
policy.ts and quote.ts no longer contain their own parsers.
Valid amounts round-trip through parse and format unchanged.

findings.summary: The gate is deny-by-default and supports both `maxTotalValue` and `allowedPeers`, and both are enforced. `autoApprove: true` with neither bound is still permitted, so an operator can opt into unbounded signing.
